But you know that a very serious shareholder with a good reputation, whose reputation we are trying to protect, its the State General Reserve Fund of the Sultanate of Oman, from the outset until the appointment of their special consultant EPIC from Vienna, they too have been talking about state aid. There is no way this can be solved without a decision of the Government, substantiated by the relevant powers and decisions of the National Assembly. Broadcaster: So, are you now thinking about what meetings should be held after the date of 5 October when general elections will take place and when a new government will take office? Ivan Iskrov: We are thinking about everything. And we not only think but we publicly announce it on our website. It is something else if you as mass media, I do not mean your particular television but the Bulgarian media in general, pay enough attention to these press releases. But Ive made a check for this interview. Since 20 June we have published 27 press releases, 22 press releases out of these are about the conservators work, KTB, Victoria, decisions of the Governing Council, etc. Therefore, everything has been announced, and I see no reason why I should repeat it all. If you wish, I could make a summary. Broadcaster: Actually, yes, about the conservators  What have they found out? Because you know that the BNB management has been much criticised of hesitating to seek solutions and of not taking a general stance? Ivan Iskrov: The BNB has never hesitated to seek a solution. I reiterate  in the very beginning the BNB, in consultation with the European Commission and the then Government of the Republic of Bulgaria, offered a possible solution. As the politicians, being in a strong pre-election confrontation, were then unwilling to back up such a solution, we continued strictly following the procedures prescribed in the Law on Credit Institutions. We may not exceed the laws authority. We may not do something different from what is written in the law. This is what the conservators are doing. Why were they late (this criticism I detect in your question, right?)? Well, they were late for reasons beyond their control. Do you forget that we... because our press release of 11 July is still on our website, in Bulgarian and in English, and is read all over the world... We, when announcing the results of the interim audit, the review of assets and liabilities, explicitly pointed out that the auditors had been unable to do their job for lack of or for incomplete information on the loan portfolio of BGN 3.5 billion, i.e. over 60% of the loan portfolio! I could give an example for your viewers to understand me better. Imagine you were selling your house. You invited me to buy the house. You wanted me to buy the house but at the same time you kept, say, three of the five rooms in the house locked up and did not let me view them. You did not give me a title deed or a scheme of the property. Well, how could I be able to assess your house and make a deal with you?! More or less, this has happened to the conservators. So they found themselves in a situation where they had to seek additional human resources, including legal advice, and throughout August they had to try and restore the missing part of the loan portfolio so that the auditors could possibly review it, and, by 20 October, next month, we could have the final auditors assessment. These are the facts, and I do not understand why the so called experts, I always mention them in inverted commas, who go around the morning TV programmes and give interviews, always forget them. Broadcaster: And what do conservators say, Mr Iskrov? Is it true that a very large percentage of the credit portfolio, nearly 90% of KTBs borrowers, is connected persons? Ivan Iskrov: Well, I wouldnt go into details on numbers, because the report here, in front of me, is public. So, your viewers could go to the website and read the whole of it. Indeed, its been cleared of the information which constitutes bank secrecy  specific firms, persons, etc. In any case, what they have written there points to such phenomena in Corporate Commercial Bank. And respectively, they are not just any people: they are good professionals and bear responsibility for what they have written. Broadcaster: Yes. Now, in view of all we are talking about, I will go a step back to ask a question and recap. What do experts say: either recovery, whether by state funding and state aid for the bank, or revoking its license, which is, in other words, declaring bankruptcy. Does this mean that the bank will no longer exist? Which do you believe is the more reasonable option at todays point? Ivan Iskrov: The Bulgarian National Bank, and its Governor in particular, has from the very first day believed that a large systemic bank of the scale of Corporate Commercial Bank, with so many customers whose funds are blocked, should be recovered as quickly as possible. Not by chance have we worked on weekends for a month. We had young women fainted in front of their computers. It wasnt accidental that colleagues of yours from other media shot with their cameras bankers, MPs and other experts going in or out, or around the head office building even on weekends. Anyway, this did not happen. Whether it will happen does not depend on the Central Bank, but on the outcome of the talks between the shareholders who stated their wish to see the bank recovered, represented by EPIC, and the Bulgarian Ministry of Finance. Respectively, it also depends on whether there will be parliamentary support to a possible positive opinion of the Bulgarian government. If they do not receive such support, it is obvious that the Central Bank would not be the authority to take a decision to dispose of taxpayers money. Of course, this is a possible solution and a good one for all depositors. In any case, Ill take the opportunity being here to say it again: insured depositors have no reason to worry at all. Things may have been slow for reasons beyond our or the Bulgarian Deposit Insurance Funds control, but they are guaranteed and will have their money back. Even if a point is reached where the banks license is to be revoked and guaranteed deposits be repaid, which we have always considered as the worst variant, but I would say it again  it does not depend on the Central Bank; the political forces in the new 43rd National Assembly will step in and have their say. Why? Because we all know that in the final run it is the responsibility of the State and the State will add this 1 billion and a half to the accumulated contributions in the Fund which are needed to repay all guaranteed deposits. So, people should not worry. Broadcaster: Since we are going into details exactly for the sake of depositors who, as you, by the way, are aware, are now protesting just beneath your office windows, does this upset you (Im asking this as a side question)? Ivan Iskrov: Its not pleasant and its not fair because the person leading them, he knows who I refer to, is leading them to the wrong site. The Central Bank is not the place protesters should go: they should rather go to the office buildings of those who led to these events, those who obstructed the bank from opening sooner. And unpleasant it is, sure enough. Broadcaster: Regarding these details that are now splitting society apart: are you ready to compensate people up to the full amount of deposits or to guarantee deposits of up to BGN 196 thousand? What is your opinion on this? Ivan Iskrov: On the previous question I commented: the Central Bank cannot answer this one either. The political will beyond what the law provides for is expressed and will be expressed by the political forces that we will elect for the 43rd National Assembly. What the currently existing law says is that upon license revocation the Bulgarian Deposit Insurance Fund must choose a bank through which within 20-days it would pay out all guaranteed deposits of up to BGN 196 thousand. Now, Ill take the opportunity here, because of the great many ill-intentioned experts, including some expert committees, which emerged claiming that there were many instruments and the BNB did not do its work, and that it could open the bank, I take the opportunity to say that one such instrument they are talking about, as for instance a substitution of the non-guaranteed portion above BGN 196 thousand with some kind of equity or financial instruments, etc., that is impossible under the currently effective legislation. If they believe that this could happen, they should write a letter to the Governor, which I would immediately make public, saying: Mr Governor, you are wrong, on the grounds of article so-and-so from law so-and-so, you can substitute Mr Vezhdi Rashidovs deposit with shares. The Bulgarian National Bank couldnt possibly do that, just as it is impossible for the Bulgarian National Bank to provide liquidity whereby to open that bank. Also, this is, because of lack of knowledge or even intentionally, a lie that is spread so that people would go to the BNB instead of somewhere else. Broadcaster: Because you mentioned a couple of times the 43rd National Assembly, Mr Iskrov, I feel tempted to ask you: Is it with relief that you are looking forward to its coming? Are you going to act ahead of events or will you be waiting for the MPs from the next National Assembly to relieve you from office? Ivan Iskrov: It is with relief that I look forward to the 43rd National Assembly, as far as the whole society needs reassurance. I hope that the 43rd National Assembly, and the people in it, would be somewhat wiser than those in the 42nd National Assembly. Broadcaster: What if you get relieved from your office? Ivan Iskrov: As regards the position of Governor, whether I would resign or not is a personal matter, which depends on me and I have always said that I know to bear a responsibility, and if I decide that I dont want to bear responsibility and be more at ease and not be accountable to society, I would inform all of you in a motivated letter. As regards, I would say, the gaffes of some candidate members of Parliament threatening to have the Governor replaced, I would like to tell them that these matters are very clearly provided for in the Law on the Bulgarian National Bank. I would recommend them reading still further: let them read the overarching Law which is called Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Let them read it and learn how a governor is relieved from office and what the consequences are. This is an issue which at this point I dont want to discuss. Id rather urge concentrating all our efforts and I declare that Ill be here until the KTB problem is resolved, because I want the best solution to be found, and I, my deputies, the other Governing Council members and the directors who are working incessantly here want the best solution to be found for the KTB group and its customers. Broadcaster: Yes, but only three months ago you had a perfect reputation, and something very important  so did the banking system in the country. How do you feel now? Have you got the suspicion that you were betrayed by your former friends, bankers, financiers, politicians or MPs? Ivan Iskrov: Well, Im not a naive person to feel either very much protected or very much betrayed by anyone. What I can tell you while looking into your eyes and sitting here in front of you calmly, is that I dont feel uneasy about anything I and this Bank have dove over these 11 years. Weve done our best so all of you, seven and a half million Bulgarian people, can sleep peacefully and we have proved we are doing well enough. A single case with a more peculiar bank, as a high government official called it, cannot eliminate everything altogether. Throw the baby with the bath water, as the saying goes. Dont forget that the world has gone through a very severe crisis. Bulgaria was badly affected by this crisis. Remember the panic in late 2008 with the Lehman Brothers failure and the prompt reactions of the Bulgarian National Bank at that point to calm down the market and the people. Remember the serious crisis which Europe experienced and is still experiencing. Nothing happened. Remember the forebodings of a number of institutions, an ex prime minister including, of how the euro would disintegrate the next day, how the Greek banks would go bankrupt, etc. And nothing of this happened. Do you think that these results were possible without and regardless of the efforts of all these people working at the Bulgarian National Bank, forget about the Governor, but these dozens of people working here? So, lets not generalise because of what happened with KTB. I take pride in what the Central Bank does, and one sentence about the condition of the banking sector because I can see you would be interested to hear. KTB is an isolated case. This is at least the tenth time Ive said this. The banking sector operates normally, except from 20 to 29 June when absolutely artificial tension was created to which the media and politicians with their ill-considered statements contributed quite a bit. You remember our appeal to all media and political factors to refrain from announcements Broadcaster: So thats why the law was amended. Ivan Iskrov: Well... I dont remember of what law amendment you are talking about, but then an absolutely artificial tension was injected into the Bulgarian banking sector and particular banks. Luckily, the problems dissipated and already since July weve seen restored confidence and again deposit growth. In the preliminary data, which I, as a Governor, have the privilege to know two-three days in advance, because they need to be processed before they can be published, you will see no later than next week that deposits in the banking system drastically picked up in August as well by more than one billion lev. So, the system is functioning. If banks suffer anything, its the absence of good projects to finance. Therefore, I ask you and through you also your colleagues from the other media: be careful, especially when inviting different experts who intimidate people all the time  fear-mongers. Lets not create additional problems, which are totally unneeded. Broadcaster: We started this conversation, Mr Iskrov, with the words that without doubt KTB is one of the most electrifying topics for the public. Lets finish this conversation also with the words of the Prosecutor General, Mr Tsatsarov, said in our programme, that KTB had in fact many jewellers and he hopes they would be shown and brought to light at last. Being the man who receives information before all others, do you know who the jewellers of this operation are? Ivan Iskrov: I know lots of things. You know that the Governor is among the well informed people in the Republic of Bulgaria. I can see them just like the Prosecutor General does. We see these jewellers almost daily in the morning programmes and some of them in the newspapers but I would not go into details, all the more so that the Prosecutor General uses the methods of preliminary investigation and pre-trial proceedings, so that he is better informed and I have no reason to doubt what he said. Most likely, interesting things will be coming to light. Broadcaster: One final question: Were there any worries that the European Commission would initiate an infringement procedure against Bulgaria? Ivan Iskrov: This is outside the competencies of the Central Bank. You mean when deposits are to be repaid, right? Broadcaster: Yes, yes. Ivan Iskrov: If you have questions, you should refer them to the colleague  the Chairperson of the Bulgarian Deposit Insurance Fund. What I can say, and has already been said by me and Mr Porozhanov in a letter to the Director General for Internal Market, is on the website. We have clearly explained what our legislation is. That some officials in the Commission see things otherwise, let them substantiate their view, lets sit down and discuss it. But if the Commission does not find a common ground with the country, its nothing to fear. Thats what the Luxembourg Court of Justice is for: to decide who is right and who is wrong. If it decides that they are right, then I would again say: the 43rd National Assembly and the government to come will have the opportunity to amend the Law on Deposit Insurance. But to date, what I would like people to know so that they do not have to worry and needlessly write letters, protest, etc., the legislation is clear. The Bulgarian Deposit Insurance Fund starts repaying the guaranteed portion within 20 days of revoking the license of a commercial bank. Whether that would happen with Corporate Commercial Bank and its subsidiary Victoria is very early to say. The current shareholders have stated wishes, may these be serious, and we will support them. There are politicians, I say it again, who would have their say as to whether there would be state aid or not, and only then would a decision be taken. Broadcaster: Mr Iskrov, I thank you for this interview. Ivan Iskrov: I thank you too. Have a nice day! PAGE \* MERGEFORMAT1

Title: Statement at the Opening of the Annual Meetings of the IMF and World Bank Group Constituencies, Sofia, May 30, 2015.
text: Statement by Mr. Ivan Iskrov, BNB Governor, at the Opening of the Annual Meetings of the IMF and World Bank Group Constituencies, Sofia, 30 May 2015 Dear Ministers and Governors, Ladies and Gentlemen, It is my pleasure and honour on behalf of the BNB to welcome all of you to this years meetings of the IMF and World Bank Group constituencies in Sofia. It is a long-standing practice for these meetings each year to be hosted by a different member country. I would like to recall that Bulgaria last hosted such a meeting in the already distant 1999. Since that time, so many and so profound changes have taken place in our countries. In this period our IMF constituency has grown. After the 2010 IMF governance reforms our constituency comprises 15 countries already. This makes it the largest European constituency and the second largest altogether, after the United States. Our groups share amounts to 6.57% as an overall share of the IMF votes. Not only the constituency as a whole but individual member countries too have gone through historic changes since 1999. The very geopolitical map of this part of the world was changing before our eyes. That was particularly obvious in this side of Europe where four countries of our constituency  Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus and Romania  joined the EU and one of them  Cyprus  joined the euro area. Today one of the largest countries in our constituency, Ukraine, has also set out on the strategic road to EU accession and market reforms. Our members from Central and Eastern Europe have seen serious institutional reforms and restructuring as part of the processes of transition, preparation for EU membership and integration into the European and global economic and political space. Radical economic reform policies were pursued in our region  for instance those related to privatisation, making labour markets flexible, economic liberalisation, attracting foreign investments, and combatting corruption and public sector inefficiency. Since the last meeting in Sofia, our economies have gone through several business cycles. Many of the countries in our group have made significant economic progress. The following data is very indicative. From 1999 to 2014, cumulative real GDP growth in the individual countries from our constituency ranged from 25% in the Netherlands to 186% in Armenia. Please note that this period coincided with the most severe global crisis in decades. Since 1999, cumulatively our economies attracted foreign direct investments of over USD 2 trillion in total, while their direct investments in other countries totalled USD 1.9 trillion. As seen from the UNCTAD data, Belgium attracted the greatest amount of foreign direct investments in this period (nearly USD 995 billion), and Moldova - the least (slightly over USD 3 billion). Belgium again made the highest amount of foreign direct investments abroad in the period (USD 863 billion), while Macedonia made the least. This statistical data also includes investments between constituency member countries. Here Bulgaria comes close to the golden mean. In the period after 1999 our total real GDP growth reached 57% and we attracted foreign direct investments of nearly USD 53 billion. Many of the countries of our IMF and World Bank constituencies have been developing in a similar historical and economic environment. At the same time, the countries and regions represented here today had to deal with their own specific challenges in recent years. Todays conference, however, brings us together with the relevance and significance of the issues we are going to discuss. The conference will focus on several important topics from the European and global agenda. The three sessions will touch on specific, and I would even say operational, issues relating to current policies, along with conceptual issues of longer-term economic and financial implications: The first session will cover the topic of investments, and mobilising private and public resources for them, as a factor for the recovery and the development of the European economies. Participants in the session will show us the role of the European Investment Bank and the Investment Plan for Europe recently announced by the European Commission (commonly known as the Juncker Plan), and with the International Finance Corporation investment toolkit. The second session will explore the issues of economic growth within the context of demographic challenges, including those related to the ageing of population. The session will discuss the policies of income distribution, balancing between what is fair and what is economically rational. The third session will deal with the work of the IMF and the World Bank on the Financial Sector Assessment Programmes (FSAPs), against the background of global changes in banking regulations and supervisory practices in the aftermath of the 2008-2009 crisis. Last year, the IMF completed a review of the FSAP framework; hence the meeting in Sofia is an excellent opportunity to discuss current aspects of conducting FSAPs in the member countries. Thus, for instance, we will discuss FSAPs in the light of issues stemming from: the new capital regime in the EU (including CRD IV); the asset quality reviews and stress tests in the banking systems; establishing the Single Supervisory Mechanism and the Single Resolution Mechanism for banks in the euro area; the communication strategies in the context of financial stability policies. I hope that today we will all benefit from a good working atmosphere and have fruitful and memorable discussions! Dear Ladies and Gentlemen, Finally, please allow me to note the particularly valuable cooperation and the excellent working relationships we had during all these years - in both our bilateral contacts with the IMF and the World Bank, and between the countries within the constituency. Looking back, now that my nearly 12 years as BNB Governor are coming to an end, I express my gratitude to the Executive Directors of the IMF and the World Bank present here, Mr. Snel and Mr. Heemskerk, to the representatives of the 15 countries from our constituency, and through them - to all their colleagues from the present or the past with whom we have been working together in previous years. Thank you for your attention. ____________ FDI data cover the period 1999 - 2013 (Source: UNCTAD). PAGE \* MERGEFORMAT1

Title: Interview with Mr. Ivan Iskrov, Manager of the BNB, in "24 Hours" newspaper, July 4, 2015.
text: Interview with the Manager of the BNB Mr. Ivan Iskrov on the 13th and 16th in "24 Hours" newspaper, July 4, 2015. Ivan Iskrov: There are no light mandates for governor of bnb A politician who goes back to banking. Isn't that what you said when you wrote the letter of resignation, Mr. Iskrov? Are our bankers independent of politicians? I was concerned that I got involved in politics because I was invited by an exceptional man, whom I care very much to this day d0 Simeon Ii. And that I do not intend to go back to politics now because I am a banker. our decisions to be guided solely by the rule of law and the interests of the country. The BNB manager of job description must work with politicians, but always be at least at arm's length from them. Explain to me this discrepancy d0 the ECB considers you a successful young governor, and in our country d0 the most guilty of all the guilty? Well, you, the media, have contributed a lot to a few people with a dubious reputation handing out daily "verdicts" on who is and who is not to blame! For me, the professional assessments of the colleagues in the banking sector, the other central banks, the ECB are also concerned. I am also excited by the implicit assessments of the millions of depositors whose savings in banks have grown over the years, are growing today d0 this is their vote of confidence in what the BNB has done on banking stability. we have witnessed a coordinated and unprecedented political, societal and media pressure, with this visibly padded and generous funding. Many people and organizations were used to denigrate the BNB to divert attention from those who acquired assets with the money of depositors, and from their associates on the left and right in politics. The ECB didn't protect you... The official position of the ECB is to refrain from public comments about the attacks and the pressures of the BNB. They are closely monitoring the situation in Bulgaria. I will tell you that in informal talks our behaviour over the last 12 months has been very high. In some Directorates of the European Commission it is different. There, unfortunately, a local lobby whose faces are known and for which banks with Bulgarian capital are a thorn in the eye. I heard a lot of flattering words from my colleagues. For them, the BNB is an example of standing up for the independence of a central bank. They understand that since June 2014 we have passed a real and very severe stress test for independence. They know that the BNB is the institution in Bulgaria that maintains financial stability and follows the long-term public interest without succumbing to pressure and conjunctural interests. they look more soberly and judge them without being tied to Bulgarian political or corporate dependencies d0 unlike many "independent" commentators here. At the same time, in Europe, they are amazed by the lack of institutional respect and aggressiveness in attacks - something that is highly atypical in European public relations. Unfortunately, our society will pay a high price for discrediting institutions for a long time. i.E. And of secondary importance is which personalities manage the BNB in a given period with all their pros and cons. Personalities, even at the highest levels, are never more important than institutions. Perhaps the organizers of the large-scale manipulation believe in the maxim that if you repeat a lie 100 times, it becomes true. However, I believe otherwise d0 that a lie repeated even 1,000 times cannot change the truth and the facts. The fact is also that KTB has shifted attention away from what bnb has done in 12 years. In my two terms as governor, we have had so many achievements and positive results that telling them would take a fewhours. with whom I had the honor of working. For example d0 preparing for the BNB's membership in the European System of Central Banks d0 a gigantic work. We haveunderwent a major transformation in the internal organization, without increasing the number of staff, but on the contrary d0 it has decreased. We have successfully opposed all sorts of provocations against the currency board. It continued to function smoothly both during the upward business cycle and in the period of the deepest crisis that affected Bulgaria. The sustainability of the board refuted many negative forecasts, including from authoritative international organizations and the expectations of speculators. We followed strict and investigative policies to maintain the stability of the banking system. Before the crisis in the years of upsurge, we urged banks to accumulate capital and liquidity buffers. We have taken measures to curb excessive credit growth and risk-taking. from the crisis. The case of KTB remained isolated. It was the "exception that proved the rule" for the financial stability of the system. I can't help but be proud of these achievements. Authoritative world publications such as The New York Times wrote that it was the shortest banking crisis in history, "evaporated within days just as suddenly as it had appeared." And what is your "reading" of the KTB case? In the summer of 2014, measures were taken to deal with violent criminal attacks and liquidity pressures on its banking system. As a consequence, the banking sector remained very high in liquidity. The case of KTB remained isolated and did not affect either the dynamics of economic growth or the rest of the sector. It is therefore incorrect to claim that in 2014 we had a banking crisis. On the contrary, it was successfully avoided. Depositors maintained confidence and their deposits continued to rise. Also, almost 100% of the covered deposits paid in KTB remained in the Bulgarian banks. With regard to the KTB Group d0 despite enormouspressure, the systematic destruction of authority and the sabotage of our actions, we were able to fulfill our tasks and make decisions based on the available and indisputable information at all times, in strict compliance with the existing legislation and beyond the divergent interests of various corporate and other lobbies. Unfortunately, we were not understood by the politicians and KTB could not be restructured and opened on 21 July. We have avoided the social tensions and the political crisis that the same problem has caused in Central and Eastern Europe. I will also mention the attraction of one of the world's largest banknote producers in Bulgaria. and very soon maybe euro banknotes. In addition, Bulgarian banknotes cost us 40% cheaper. And instead of thankingus for it, some lobbies have publicly spat on the BNB. Challenge them with facts, what else did the BNB do during your two terms? I'il tell you some telling data, i'm presenting them for the first time. From 2005 to 2015, the BNB transferred to the state budget contributions of over 2 billion euro. Lv. (o) the annual excess of revenue over expenditure for each previous year. We were able to set aside additional capital reserves for BGN 1.2 billion. Two terms at the top of the BNB. Both end in resignations. The first d0 to re-elect you, and the second d0 after squeezing from all directions. Which way after July 10? It can be said that two different parliaments have twice elected me for a second term, and when I resign before the current National Assembly, I have not been guided by thin bills, but only by preserving the interests of the BNB and the country. Are you going to the ECB? No, I'm not going to work at the ECB. Of course, I can not help but be pleased that I already have several offers both abroad and here. But first of all, I want a quick selection of a successor and its rapid introduction into the affairs of the BNB. Before you go to sleep, should I take you back to the sleepless nights of 2008d02009. There's nolight mand8e for the central bank manager. Only within days, interbank interest rates in bulgaria rose to 6.4%. Big financial players tried to shake the board through massive short selling of Bulgarian global bonds. You did it discreetly because the banking system is sensitive... But by one big difference d0 then I had a responsible and predictable political class behind the backs of the BNB and the Ministry of Finance. While 2014 was the exact opposited0 a dysfunctional parliament and the collapse of government, the departure of the main political players from any responsibility and attempt to transfer all the lones to the BNB. Some political leaders were willing to waste, for their personal and part-time interests, the difficult financial stability of the last 20 years. In the middle ages, in some cities during the plague, those incapable of dealing with and fearing the discontent of the people were found guilty of witches and sneered. they have a lot to explain d0 about the growth of this bank during the years of their managements, its connection with entire sectors of the economy, as well as their financial relations with the bank in question and its majority owner. even less political bias. In both 2008 and 2014, and today the BNB works professionally, noise-free for financial stability in Bulgaria. They say that if the transcripts of the meetings with the president are opened, interesting things willbe seen. I categorically do not wish to comment on names and political subjects. At least not to date. The initial ideas and plans related to KTB after its placement under special supervision on 20 June 2014 are publicly known. So I would hardly say anything unknown. But I would recall that the BNB proposed a plan agreed with the government and the EC and initially supported by the parliamentary parties. (a) a 'good' bank, assets which can be assessed to be in good condition and able to generate income of the bank, as well as KTB's liabilities, with the exception of those relating to the main shareholder, to move to the balance sheet of Commercial Bank Victoria. as promised. To emphasise another d0 there was an opportunity for their funds to receive depositors with amounts above the legally guaranteed 196 thousand euro. Lv. Unfortunately, genderintrigue then thwarted this plan. The impression was clearly made, and I am convinced that the majority shareholder also seriously used his political friendships against BNB. The plan in question followed the models that have already been successfully implemented in other countries. together with the BNB, agree on the case resolution strategy. However, the plan required parliament to adopt new legislation with bank resolution tools that it did not have at the time. Someone else accepted it. To drop banking secrecy for politicians in the face of bank failure. Do you approve of it? It has already been adopted, i.e. this is not a topic that the BNB should comment on at this stage. But I would allow myself a personal view d0 that the disclosure of the information will confirm the vicious scheme established by the BNB and the Quaestors for the robbery of KTB depositors by the majority shareholder. banking secrecy in the case of KTB will eventually reveal what all open-minded observers understand d0 KTB ceased to exist as a result of the actions of its majority shareholder and the management of this bank, not because of BNB. which then turned out to have been transferred outside the balance sheet of KTB, there would not have been a capital shortfall, when we were legally obliged to revoke the license. Stress tests are forthcoming for our banks and valuation of their assets. Opinions are polar, divided. From d0 this will bring back confidence in the banking system, to d0 whatever the results, people will always say, come on, come on you fooled us. What do you think will happen? Bnb announced last year that it intends to initiate a review of the quality of the assets of all banks in Bulgaria, including stress tests. The methodology for the stress tests will be based on the best ECB standards applied to the major banks in the euro area in 2014. Some argue that stress tests are necessary to "restore" confidence in our banking system. In2014, there was no banking crisis in Bulgaria, and citizens' deposits continued to grow. Look south of us to see what the citizens' trust in the banks means. However, asset quality review and stress testingare necessary because they would be a key requirement if the government at some stage started a conversation with the ECB about Bulgaria joining the so-called Single Supervisory Mechanism of the euro area. Did the BNB seem to have a negative view ofswift accession to european single supervision? No, you're not mistaken! Single supervision is one of the elements of the Banking Union. BNB and the Ministry of State were involved in the discussions that led to its establishment. We strongly supported deepening integration in the euro area, including But, at the same time, we and other countries have insisted on equal treatment of countries within and outside the euro area. Title: Interview before "Capital" newspaper
text: Interview with the Manager of the BNB Mr. Dimitar Radev before "Capital" newspaper, July 25, 2015. Dimitar Radev was born on July 12, 1956. During his 21-year career there, he rose to deputy minister in charge of the budget process. In2001, Radev appeared in a competition at the International Monetary Fund, where he subsequently worked for 14 years. Kostov, Kalin Hristov and Nina Stoyanova, as well as the arguments for their expertise and experience in the central bank, are opposed to accusations of moral responsibility for the sleep of the KTB case  something they claim was entirely in the court of "encapsulated" banking supervision. to vote against. You return to Bulgaria after a successful career at the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to take over as Governor of the BulgarianNational Bank (BNB). The invitation came from Prime Minister Borisov. I understand that it is the result of a long survey of a small number of candidates, based on twocreeds of competence and independence. This profile perfectly coincides with my understanding of what the central bank governor should be, so this was the main motivation to accept. Were there any demands on you, or was the invitation tocome and run a bank as you see it? There were no preconditions. Obviously, public expectation is now focused on banking supervision in particular. Corporate Commercial Bank (KTB) was a failure that was somewhat acknowledged by the BNB itself in its post-bankruptcy reports. What is your analysis of the situation with KTB? It's definitely a failure of banking supervision and I don't think anyone denies that. The problems from the BNB's point of view are actually two: first, banking supervision, and secondly, the lack of an instrument to solve such crises. This has also become clear as a result of the KTB crisis. And therefore my focus is on these two main directions: to reform banking supervision and to create a framework forresolving such crises. In the public consciousness, KTB is an example of political corruption. Do you see one in this case? How can it be solved and how can it be eradicated from the banking system if it is available? I know the problems are complex. I think the BNB should be completely insulated from all political influences. Of course, for both the political class and commercial banks, there are lessons that they can learn from theKTB case. There are reasonable doubts that practices similar to those in KTB can be found in other banks. How do you plan to cure the system? By reforming banking supervision. The most secure guarantee is the integration of the risk of such practices into the overall risk assessment of each bank. This will determine the frequency and scope of the checks. The higher the risk assessment, the more frequent the checks will be. What is the picture of the banking sector that you had when you took office? Some things are obvious - the indicators are down to capital adequacy and liquidity. And this preliminary analysis, which you are preparing for September, is it related to your suspicions of problems in the banking sector that are not clear in the reports? In fact, what we will do by the end of September is assessbanking supervision. In a way, the assessment of banking supervision should have already been carried out by the IMF. There was a request for an FSAP procedure for the evaluation of theentire bank system. Here we are talking about three groups of measures and processes that I presented in my concept when I was elected governor of the BNB. First, this is the assessment of banking supervision by the IMF and the World Bank. This process will be completed by the end of July 2016. confidence in the BNB and the banking sector. And aren't these deadlines very stretched against the backdrop of public outingsfor swift action, including what was objectively objective in the European Commission's report? Our deadlines are realistic, even tense. There are established international practices and internal procedures that objectify these deadlines. Inorder to assess the quality of assets, for example, only the choice of BNB consultants to be made under the Public Procurement Act will take three months. All steps must be in the correct order. Before finalising the asset quality assessment, we must have answers to the potential questions it may put. I expect the Bank Recovery and Resolution Act to be adopted soon. respond to the results of the evaluations we will receive next year. So, for example, the July 2016 deadline for asset quality assessment is completely re-allist and even tense. We have strong arguments and I think we will reach an agreement with the European Commission. Has Brussels already communicated on the subject? This is the deadline that is set in the national reform programme adopted by the government, which has been sent to the EC. The details will be commented on in my first contacts with our partners inBrussels on this topic, of course, in agreement with the government and the Ministry of Finance. After the collapse of KTB, the group of companies associated with DPS MP DelyanPeevski started to actively finance four smaller banks. There will be no special treatment for any bank in either direction: neither easing nor stricter supervision. This will be the approach, regardless of who the shareholder is, what is the capital, private or state. But at the same time, as I pointed out,the depth and depth of the checks will depend on the risk assessment for each bank. So will the BDB also be covered by the checks? Naturally. An important issue related to the checks is that the entire supervisory plan has been severely reduced in the last year. contactedone bank or another. Is there a need to change staff policy, direct more resources, purely human, to banking supervision? A lot of change is needed. In our plan, by the end of September, we will specify these tasks, including with regard to the necessary human resources. For example, we currently only have five on-site surveillance teams. We're assessing whether that's enough. We will probably need to create a sixth team. With Mr. Dimitar Kostov, whom I have proposed as a sub-manager in charge of banking supervision, we have full agreement on what needs to be done in banking supervision and that is why I think we will succeed. Kostov looks at your personal choice. How did you decide for the other two positions to also offer people fromivan Iskrov's team  Kalin Hristov and Nina Stoyanova? I've known Dimitar Kostov for many years. I've seen him act in very difficult, even critical situations, and I know I can totally count on him. The issue with the sub-managers is about the structure of management and decision-making in the BNB. The information specifically in the case of KTB, which has reached the other sub-managers, did not actually give rise to any reaction. replaceable. To this end, we will establish reliable channels of information and a framework for the adequate engagement of all members of the Management Board. At the same time, both Dimitar Kostov and Kalin Hristov and Nina Stoyanova have managed their respective resources perfectly. I am pleased that this opinion is shared by a wide range of representatives of the professional field. Even assuming that the information in banking supervision was fully encapsulated and did not reach the other sub-managers, at least in the years before KTB closed, there were a lot of media publications that raised serious questions. The answer they received was that there were no problems. Moreover, there was no legal framework to allow such intervention in the re-manager responsible for Banking Supervision, both directly and under the Governing Council. Does this mean that in all the years there have been no reports that theyhave signaled at least any risks in KTB, not necessarily the problems in its entirety that came out afterwards, but at least from the concentration of deposits, from a liquidity problem, if the state suddenly withdraws a large part of them? As far as I understand it, no such reports have been submitted to the Board of Directors and no such reports have been considered, but this is also subject to ongoingscrutiny by the competent authorities, including the Court of Auditors. Are you going to change the principle of liability in the BNB? Quietly, he waswith mesen from the beginning of 2007, and by the end of 1996 he was personal  to manager and sub-manager "Banking Supervision", and then transferred to the collective body  management board of BNB . As I have pointed out, the principle will be a greater commitment to the personal responsibility of all board members. This can be achieved through a more structured model of work in the BNB. One such goodworking example in the central bank is the Investment Committee related to the management of international foreign exchange reserves, which includes representatives of all managements in the BNB. In terms of your choice of sub-managers, how many people did you choose to stop at Kostov, Hristov, Stoyanova? There were extremely strong candidates who fully met these two main criteria, which I have already stated: integrity and expertise. For example, within the framework ofKalin Hristov's management, the reserves of the currency board increased from BGN 24 billion, to over 38 billion euro. Lv. Never have international foreign exchange reserves had such a high size. Payment systems work flawlessly. This is an extremely responsible and difficult task. Nina Stoyanova has done a tremendous job in relation to the regulatory framework. We are transforming the regulatory framework in line with the European requirements. You list the pros, but there are minuses. Like what? For example, one of the arguments you have heard in the assessment of Kalin Hristov is that he was a campaigner of the idea of not joining Bulgaria in the single banking supervision. This is something that is currently set as a priority in your programme. The same person who has defended one thesis will now have to move all the work of joiningthe single banking supervision. I think it's a healthy conservatism that I personally value a lot because he appreciates all the factors professionally. This is not about euro area membership and the Single Supervisory Mechanism, but about how to get to them. So I have nodifferences with Kalin Hristov and he also agrees with my concept of governance, which puts membership of the euro area as a strategic and unchanging goal. When do you think Bulgaria should submit an application for single banking supervision? There are two moments here  there are a few steps before this can be done. They are coming into the formal requirements of this close cooperation mechanism. One step is to complete the asset quality assessment, so that this cannot be done before the environment of the following year. The other issue is to re-evaluate all the factors and this will be done within the newly created Coordination Council for joining the euro area, in which the BNB will participate very actively. Bnb will focus on the issues, contactus with the single banking union, and will be guided primarily by the interests of the country, not by political or other conjunctural considerations. And does it bother you that the support for the sub-governors you have proposed can actually be reached in a situation where they can only be elected with the votes of GERB and DPS? I do not know, I do not want to speculate on this topic, because I have not discussed the issue with parliamentary groups. Some have steadfastly stated that they would not support a candidate who was in the previous administration. I fully understand and respect the positions of parliamentary groups and their political decisions on this issue. With the same degree of respect, however, I do not agree with the entirely politically motivated arguments. I am looking at things from a purely professional point of view. These nominations are based entirely on professional, technocratic criteria. At the same time, I am very aware that at some stage this professional approach must find a pr essay point with the political agenda of the various parliamentary groups. that they will ultimately support the nominations because the professional arguments are strong enough. If, after all, it comes down to not supporting any of the candidates, willyou feel it as a withdrawal of political trust from you? I have received broad political support in my election and now I do not want to speculate on this topic. Do you have a plan B if nominations don't get support in parliament? I'm 100% focused on Plan A. How do you imagine the BNB and the banking sector at the end of your term of office after six years? Where do you expect the country's banking system to go? I expect there to be a period of consolidation in the banking sector within my mandate. A modern banking sector,consolidated on a market basis, will be a key factor for financial stability and economic growth. The interview can be seen HYPERLINK " /" \t "_top" here. Title: Interview for Bloomberg
Subtitle: Governor, what are Bulgarias economic prospects for Bulgaria with all the surrounding crises? The Ukranian conflict, the Russian sanctions, the Syrian war, the unprecedented influx of migrants to Europe, instability in neighbouring Greece  how is all this affecting Bulgarian economy and its prospects?
text: Interview of the BNB Governor Mr. Dimitar Radev for Bloomberg, 17 November 2015 Governor, what are Bulgarias economic prospects for Bulgaria with all the surrounding crises? The Ukranian conflict, the Russian sanctions, the Syrian war, the unprecedented influx of migrants to Europe, instability in neighbouring Greece  how is all this affecting Bulgarian economy and its prospects? Unfortunately, global and regional risks to the economic outlook have increased, and the tragic events in Paris last week rendered a new dimension to these risks. We monitor closely and try to react adequately to these developments. For example the preemptive measures by the Central Bank in coordination with the government mitigated substantially the risks for our banking system from the economic crisis in Greece. The macroeconomic impact from the other risks you are referring to are also limited at this stage. However, as a result of this unfavourable environment we expect that economic growth will remain below its potential, at least in the near term. How realistic in your opinion is the governments projection of economic growth of 2.1% for next year? The Central Bank does not have any major differences with the government in assessing macroeconomic developments. We project economic growth of about 2% this year, supported by robust export performance and better utilisation of the EU funds, mainly through the public investment program. Turning to 2016, we expect strengthening of domestic demand, driven by the private sector, which will help keep economic growth in line with this years level, and even marginally increase it. Just to make sure  you expect 2% economic growth for this year or for 2016? We expect 2% for this year and marginally increasing the next year to 2.1% and even slightly higher. How achievable is the governments plan to narrow the budget deficit next year, after an estimate of 3.3% for this year? It is worth mentioning that the 3.3% budget deficit, as announced, is the internal cash base measure for the fiscal balance. On a comparable basis, the ESA-compliant figure will be below 3%. Overall fiscal performance this year has been strong mainly as a result of the better than expected revenue which created some space for different policy choices, for making additional savings, which from the Central Banks perspective will be the preferable one, or making additional spending to cover urgent mainly one-off needs. Of course the decision is entirely within the discretion of the government. The bottom line is that the budget deficit is expected to remain within the 3% mark, which is a good starting point for further strengthening the consolidation effort and narrowing the budget deficit to 2% next year. What is the country doing to attract more foreign investment? It has been fairly low in recent years. Its not only a Bulgarian phenomenon. Its a lot to do with the investment climate following the global financial crisis. There are clear signs this year that this trend is changing, and if you analyze the regional data, youll figure out that in fact direct investments in Bulgaria, as a share of GDP, are higher in comparison to the so called new Member States in terms of both inflows and size of the stock. This been said, we know that more remains to be done at our end. The good news is that broad political support is emerging for reforms, including in the judiciary, but also in sectors such as energy and transport that accumulated contingent liabilities in the past. When is Bulgaria planning to adopt the euro? Well, I think the answer to this question is in our Accession Treaty - when all the necessary conditions are fulfilled. This is not yet the case. While the official criteria are well within reach, more remains to be done on the structural front, including by resolving the remaining issues in the state-owned enterprises sector and ensuring the fiscal sustainability of the health and pension systems. The Finance Minister Mr. Goranov has mentioned 2018 as the date to join the ERM II. How realistic do you think this is, and have any specific steps been taken by the Bulgarian authority to join ERM II? As a Central Bank we mainly focus on the pre-requisites, and here Im referring to three groups of measures - first, strengthening banking supervision; second, introducing a bank recovery and resolution framework and making it operational; and third, carrying out an asset quality review and stress tests of our banks. Weve already adopted, published and implement these measures. Our plan is to complete their implementation by the end of 2016, and then well probably be clear about the specific timeline for joining the ERM II. So 2018 at the moment is it a realistic target or is something yet to be discussed? I dont think that defining a specific deadline will be very productive at this stage, will probably be premature. So we want to see first how these measures will be implemented, what the outcomes will be, specifically from the asset quality review and the stress tests of our banking system. And, then, we can further discuss the specific steps and the timeline for their implementation. Have there been any discussions of changing the lev-euro exchange rate in Bulgaria? No. Our position on this is crystal clear. Joining the eurozone is the only exit strategy from the current fixed euro-lev exchange rate. How stable is Bulgarias banking system after the collapse of Corporate Commercial Bank last year and what actions has the Central Bank taken to improve bank supervision? I think our banking system is generally stable, liquid and well capitalised. The collapse of the CCB last year revealed certain weaknesses in our banking supervision practices. Thats why strengthening banking supervision is in the centre of our reform efforts. Our Banking Supervision Department is under major reorganisation. We plan further steps to improve its capacity and its practices in line with the Basel Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision. What is the level of non-performing loans in Bulgaria and how do you see their resolution? The level of non-performing loans has stabilised this year below 11 billion leva on a gross basis and it has adequate coverage in terms of provisions of over 50%. On top of the provisions we have a capital surplus in the system of about 7.1 billion leva as of September. A number of measures are under implementation, including sales of groups of loans and balance sheet write-offs as a result of the realisation of collateral. And I expect that as a result of the coming AQR and stress tests there will be additional impulse in this direction. And what is your expectation of the outcome of the stress tests in the Bulgarian banking system next year? I expect that the stress tests will confirm that our banking system overall is sound. Of course, we are working very hard to be fully prepared also for less favourable scenarios and here I mainly mean what we are doing in the banking supervision area, including by enforcing a rules-based approach and improving internal controls in banking supervision, but also addressing remaining gaps in our resolution framework, and, last but not least, providing a proper backstop for potential capital shortfalls in individual banks where the shortfalls cannot be covered from the market. And what would be a least favourable scenario in this situation? A least favourable scenario would be if as a result of the stress tests we figure out that we have systemic problems in the banking system. I dont believe this would be the case, however, but of course, as I mentioned, some problems are possible in individual banks and we are fully prepared to address these problems. Do you see any bank mergers or acquisitions planned in the near future in the Bulgarian banking system? I expect market consolidation would be one of the strategic directions in which our banking sector will develop but at this stage its a bit early to be very specific about this issue. What book are you reading in your leisure time? You probably saw they just gave me this book that I want to read and I think it will help me in my communication with the press  its Umberto Ecos Numero Zero. Title: Interview for the show "This Morning" on BTV
text: Interview with the Manager of the BNB Mr. Dimitar Radev for the show "This Morning" on B TV, 4 December 2015. The Governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, Mr. Dimitar Radev, gave an interview on the tv show "This Morning" on BV TV. He commented on topical issues related to the activities of the Central Bank and financial stability in the country. One of rossi'smain ups was related to the upcoming valuation of banks' assets and the stress tests to be carried out in 2016. "Stress tests are a standard tool that banks themselves apply. What will happen next year will be this independent external assessment of the quality of the assets of commercial banks. Mr Radev said. The governor was also asked to comment on how he built his team at the Central Bank, as well as allegations that he had not made significant changes. The Governor pointed out that there are new holdersin the bank department, in the banking supervision department, there is also a new Secretary General, a new Chief Legal Officer and a new Chief Accountant. "These are people from the Central Bank and people from our banking sector. Most of these people have worked with two or three governors, so this is a change that the Central Bank doesn't know at least in recent decades, and I think it's being done in a very serious way. professional and balanced way, as things should be done in such an institution as the Central Bank", the Governor of the BNB was adamant. Asked if politicians were interfering in his work as governor, he said there was a state-of-the-state approach and at least since he was in that position, there had been no interference. "Decisions taken at the Central Bank shall be taken absolutely independently. And I have to say, and I think I have a duty to do so, that the tone for this state-of-the-art decision towards the Central Bank is given by both the Bulgarian Prime Minister and the most responsible political factors.", said Mr Radev. When asked if something similar to KTB could happen, the Central Bank governor replied that the banking system as a whole is stable. Anyone who monitors the indicators that the Central Bank publishes will see that our commercial banks have high liquidity, with significant capital buffers. The results of their activities and as a profit are very good. it is generally stable, but the final restoration of trust goes through what we call a review of the quality of their assets and stress tests. Mr Radev said that the evaluation would be organised in an independent way by external auditors, which is necessary not only to restore trust, but also to achieve strategic objectives, including related to euro area membership. Asked when Bulgaria would become part of the euro zone, the BNB governor said that any fixing of dates at this point would not be productive. the topics are  banking supervision, the establishment of an institutional framework for the recovery and resolution of banks and, of course, the assessment of the quality of assets in our banking sector, Mr Radev said. Title: Interview given to Kiril Vulchev for The Year on Darik Radio
Subtitle: What will be the word of the year 2016? Do you expect consolidation of banks?
text: Interview with the BNB Governor Mr. Dimitar Radev, given to Kiril Vulchev for d4The Yeard5 on Darik Radio, 12 December 2015. What will be the word of the year 2016? Do you expect consolidation of banks? I expect that what we started in the middle of 2015 will continue into 2016. So, in 2016 this word (consolidation) could be just as topical. Do you really expect consolidation of banks? Consolidation is a good word in the financial dictionary. It has several meanings. It means improvement in a countryd5s financial position. Of course, it also means what you are asking about - consolidation in the banking sector. This allows me to say that this will be one of the strategic directions in which our banking sector is going to develop. What exactly are these stress tests about? How are they carried out? Letd5s give a bit more popular explanation. Actually the main part of this exercise is what we call an assessment of commercial banksd5 assets. The stress tests will be based on that assessment of assets. They are designed to show to what extent the Bulgarian banks can act adequately under different macroeconomic conditions and with various risks involved. This is a very serious and important exercise. Many EU countries are already going through it. This is one of the challenges we will be faced with in 2016, and we are making very serious preparations so that we can carry out this asset quality review and the stress tests in the best possible way. What was the effect of the KTB case on the banking sector this year? The whole story of KTB has in fact undermined the confidence in the Bulgarian National Bank. Therefore, one of my highest priorities is winning back the confidence in the Central Bank. What should change in supervision? Many things do need to change in supervision, and these changes are already taking place. The Banking Supervision Department has undergone a very serious reorganisation aimed to enhance its efficiency, to improve the internal controls over its activities. We have implemented an annual audit system for supervisory activities, and we have also radically changed the Central Bankd5s governance with regard to banking supervision so that responsibility is vested in the entire Governing Council. What are the implications of the external threats? The 2015 events are immigrants, terrorism, wars in the Middle East, the conflicts between Russia d0 EU and Turkey, Greeced5s debt crisis. How do these events affect the finances of Bulgaria? All these events definitely create an unfavourable external environment which is stifling the potential economic growth. What we, as a country, are trying to do, I think successfully hitherto, is to reduce the adverse effects of these events. One particular example is preventing problems of Greeced5s debt crisis from spilling over into our financial system. And how do you do that? This has been done through a series of steps, including liquidity requirements for the Greek banksd5 subsidiaries, limiting the exposure to the d4parentsd5 in Greece, a number of decisions regarding their operational work, which have practically led to a situation where both the country and our banks have no exposure neither to Greek banks, nor to the Greek government. However, the idea of a negative interest rate on banksd5 excess reserves at the BNB suggests that the problem is quite the reverse d0 banks seem to prefer keeping their money in Bulgaria because it is safe and at the same time itd5s been profitable up to now? That is true and itd5s part of a bigger issue. A few days ago the ECB made a decision to extend its Quantitative Easing programme, as they call it, related to the purchase of government bonds in the secondary market until March 2017. The same decision lowered the deposit facility rate by 10 basis points down to -0.3 percent. What we are doing by introducing negative interest rates on banksd5 excess reserves is actually a reflection of these processes. We have higher liquidity in the system. The demand for loans is still not adequate. So this is a complex issue and we are keeping close watch on it. What is the amount of deposits with the Bulgarian banks in 2015? Deposits tend to increase and amount to around BGN 62 billion, out of which BGN 41 billion is household deposits. What kind of signal is this to the economy? People prefer to keep their money on deposit and earn interest rather than do business. The signals are not unambiguous. On the one hand, this is a sign of trust in the banking system. On the other hand, this increasing liquidity indicates the banking systemd5s potential to support the economic activity, which however does not meet with the relevant demand. What is the volume of lending in 2015? There are no specific trends up or down. Total loans amount to around BGN 50 billion, including around BGN 18 billion to households. What does this mean? There is BGN 60 billion in banks, and they have lent BGN 50 billion of it. Generally speaking, yes. There is over BGN 10 billion available on deposit. This is not precisely how we calculate it. There is substantial liquidity which can be used. The big question here is d0 what will happen next year? In my view, this trend of interest rate levels will continue, especially in the context of the ECBd5s decision that I mentioned. You expect that the rates on deposits and loans would go down? The general trend is a downward one. It is very important to note that the correlation between deposit rates and loan rates will not be, and may not be, automatic because banks, when granting loans, must also assess the level of credit risk. Is the currency board arrangement stable? The currency board arrangement is stable. We will finish this year with historically the largest total assets number on the Issue Department balance sheet d0 nearly BGN 40 billion. The currency board arrangement is now covered by international foreign exchange reserves at over 150 percent. The future of the currency board arrangement is also clear. It will remain in place until we adopt the euro. When will this happen? It is clearly a political decision. The most precise answer is to be found in our agreement with EU, which sets out that we will adopt the euro when all conditions for this are met. I think that the right focus now is on these conditions d0 we know which these conditions are in the banking sector and in the economy in general d0 and not in settling specific dates. Is that how the currency board would have looked like, had Bulgaria not taken new debts this year? Is taking new debts a positive or a negative? I think that taking new debts has no direct bearing on and does not jeopardise the currency board stability. Debts are a direct function of fiscal deficits and should be viewed exactly from this perspective. There are two positive facts when speaking about our debt level. It is among the lowest in EU. That is the first positive fact. The second one is the clear commitment of the government, of the Ministry of Finance to fiscal consolidation and reducing deficit, which is a guarantee that debt will stay within these percentages of GDP. What sign is the 2-lev coin for Bulgariad5s finances? Some say that as paper levs become coins, then the currency must be losing value. No, that is not correct. The only sign is that we want to optimise the cash circulation costs. The durability of banknotes is a little over 1 year, so a great number of banknotes need to be print, whilst that of coins can reach up to 30 years. That reduces the overall cash circulation costs and this is the only sign. There is nothing else or any other meaning behind minting the new 2-lev coin. Which is the word of the year 2016? The same with which I started: consolidation. In my case, Id5ve been looking at things since the middle of July when I came back to this country and assumed my current position. I think consolidation is the word of the year 2016. 1
