Subtitle:
THE ASSET QUALITY REVIEW AND 
THE STRESS TEST OF THE BANKING SYSTEM IN 2016
text: Publication of Mr. Dimitar Radev, BNB Governor, in the Quarterly Bulletin of the Association of Banks in Bulgaria, issue 44, January 2016 THE ASSET QUALITY REVIEW AND THE STRESS TEST OF THE BANKING SYSTEM IN 2016 The Asset Quality Review /AQR/ followed by the stress tests for the whole banking system are going to be performed this year. The AQR is a result of the mandate granted to the BNB by 9 of the Transitional and Final Provisions of the Law on the Recovery and Resolution of Credit Institutions and Investment Firms, adopted last year. The BNB shall organise the AQR of the banking system, including a review of the quality and adequacy of estimates used to value assets, collateral received, impairment and provisioning practices with involvement of independent external persons with high professional reputation. The review is going to be done in direct cooperation with the European Commission and the European Banking Authority and it is going to be based on the methodology corresponding to the one that has been already applied by the European Central Bank in the run up to the Single Supervisory Mechanism in the euro area in 2014. The process has already started in accordance with a plan which includes the period between the summer of 2015 and the end of 2016. That period of 18 months was announced at my election as a Governor of the BNB and the concrete measures and deadlines were institutionalised after their approval by the BNB Governing Council in the autumn of 2015. The AQR and the stress test for the banking system aims to meet two groups of challenges: (1) related to the confidence in the Central bank and in the banking sector after the Corporate Commercial Bank case; and (2) related to the strategic decisions which shall be undertaken by Bulgaria regarding its accession to the euro area and its full integration in the European supervisory and financial architecture. The BNB expects that the AQR and the stress tests are going to confirm the stability of the banking sector as a whole. At the same time we shall be ready to react to concrete problems in case they appear. Contrary to 2014, today there is an established and institutionalised framework for crises management in the sector, both regarding the stronger role on prevention performed by the banking supervision as well as the regulation of the banks resolution processes (by the newly created legal framework on recovery and resolution of credit institutions). The AQR is not just a goal in itself or an isolated exercise but it is also an element with a short-term strategic context of the tasks and challenges confronted by the BNB and the whole financial system. It aims to serve as a basis of the overall evaluation of the state of the financial sector in Bulgaria in the second half of 2016  through the so-called Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP), carried out by the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. After the finalisation of AQR and the stress test of the banking system and after the FSAP, an analysis of the necessary steps for the realisation of the strategic goals is going to be performed for the accession to the euro area and the full integration to the European supervisory and financial architecture. Then the approaches and the next steps for achieving those goals together with the possible deadlines (if they can be currently justified) are going to be defined. The proposals for the choice of approaches, phases and deadlines are going to be formulated by the Coordination Council for the preparation of Bulgarias membership in the euro area where the BNB is going to participate actively. Considering those proposals the government and the National Assembly are going to take the final decisions.

Title: Statement at the Banker weeklys Conference Lending as a Driver of Economic Growth, Sofia
text: Statement by the BNB Governor Mr. Dimitar Radev at the Banker weeklys Conference Lending as a Driver of Economic Growth, Sofia, 26 April 2016 Ladies and gentlemen, I am going to focus on four interrelated aspects of the subject of bank lending and economic growth. These are about the macroeconomic aspect, monetary policy, credit risk and the factors of economic growth. First, I will reflect on the macroeconomic dimension and the relationship between bank lending and economic growth. This is neither unequivocal, nor unidirectional. Bank lending is not the only factor of economic growth. Last year the GDP growth doubled compared to 2014, while credit growth was negative. The dynamics of lending in this specific context depends not so much on supply as on demand. In the final analysis, it is the real sector that offers and implements the projects bank lending is sought for. We should also recognize the fact that the real sectors access to funding is not limited only to bank lending. The gross operating surplus is still the main source of funding for companies in Bulgaria. Besides, many Bulgarian companies are subsidiaries of foreign ones and use credit lines from their parent companies. According to the latest data, around 50% of loans used by companies in Bulgaria are related to foreign investment and external debt in the form of intra-company loans, while bank lending accounts for 37% of the credit resources of domestic companies. Hence, the relationship between bank lending and economic growth is a complex one. The main factors for economic growth, such as investment and consumption, can be financed not only by bank credit but from also other sources of funds. The second important dimension is the relationship between monetary policy and bank lending. Under a currency board we are not in a position to pursue a discretionary monetary policy. Even central banks implementing such a policy find it difficult to achieve quick and sustainable growth of bank lending. For example, in spite of the policy of large-scale quantitative easing, pursued by the ECB, partly aimed at increasing bank lending, credit in the euro area has just revived to weak positive growth. If we come back to the situation in Bulgaria, the introduction of negative interest rates on the banks excess reserves at the BNB early this year transmits the ECBs monetary conditions and policy into our country. That decision is not a manifestation of a discretionary policy, by which the BNB would like to force banks to increase lending, but it could increase the price incentive for offering bank credit which, in turn, would increase its demand. It is clear that central banks, including the BNB, have limited ability to stimulate lending. Therefore, it is very important to realize that economic growth needs the support of many other factors, not just monetary policy. For instance, structural reforms and a balanced fiscal policy are some of the most important factors for enhancing the potential of the economy and its competitiveness, and for achieving a sustainable economic growth. The third dimension is related to risk management in banks. Banks must assess credit risk taking into account the phase of the economic cycle and must demand from borrowers an adequate price for taking that risk. When that price could not be received, it would be better if the loan were not granted. Therefore, we should not tolerate poor credit risk management just for the sake of achieving credit growth. I think that the experience of Bulgaria and other countries categorically supports the conclusion that economic growth driven primarily by lending is unhealthy. Such a growth usually comes along with the accumulation of uncovered credit risk, which is a pre-condition for imbalanced increase in the prices of some assets, such as real estate. This might jeopardize the financial stability and hence impede the economic growth itself. One of the main conclusions from the global financial crisis, and from our own experience, is that a rapid and abrupt growth in lending, especially in an uncertain macroeconomic environment, is generally a sign of poor risk management. Other countries examples aside, it will suffice to mention our own experience in 2014 of KTBs vigorous credit growth before the bank was closed. Consequently, to sum up, I would re-state that credit growth should not be achieved just for its sake and at the expense of poor credit risk management in individual banks. The worlds experience from the booming years before the global financial crisis shows that an economic growth mainly driven by credit expansion is not healthy for the economy. The fourth dimension is related to the distinction that we should make between the short-term and long-term perspective on these processes. Bank credit can be influenced by current factors, some of a cyclical nature, connected with the state of the economic environment. However, other factors and events may have an impact on lending in the long run. A current factor that is influencing lending is the uncertain economic environment. It discourages companies and households from taking new loans and even makes them want to reduce the loans they have already taken out. Another such factor is the measures undertaken by the banks to optimize their balance sheets by writing off or selling loans. At the same time, some examples of factors having a long-term effect on credit growth are the continuous decrease in interest rates on deposits and loans, the high liquidity in the banking system, and the intense competition between the banks in Bulgaria. In this context, I should not neglect to also note the asset quality review. The prevailing view is that the asset quality review and the stress test would slow down lending. The analysis of the asset quality review effect however should not be simplified. In the short term, for the asset quality review the banks have engaged a significant expert and organisational resource, which would otherwise have supported the lending activity. Another short-term effect is that the asset review encourages the banks to further focus on an adequate credit risk assessment and coverage. The economic processes, however, and the credit impact should not be assessed in isolated three or six months periods, but always within a strategic context. From this perspective, the asset review aims to achieve an independent and conservative assessment, which is necessary to fully capture the credit risk in the banking system balance sheet. Having gone through the whole process, banks should have capital to adequately cover their risk exposures. The availability of such capital coverage, coupled with the existing high liquidity in the banking system, would help banks to assume new risk. Therefore, within the medium and long-term horizon we expect a positive effect from conducting the asset quality review and the stress test. In this regard, it would be incorrect to claim that the asset review would slow down the growth in credit and the economy. To summarise whats been said so far, I would stress that bank lending is an important  but not the only  factor of economic growth. Also, apart from banks, there are other alternative sources of lending to finance investment and consumption. From this perspective, the debate on economic growth and its relationship to lending should take into account the coherence of all factors. Second, a central banks monetary policy is not sufficient to create all necessary preconditions for banking credit growth and economic growth in general, especially in the absence of discretionary monetary policy. Third, a good credit risk management is more essential than reporting positive statistics of banking credit growth as an end in itself. Last but not least, when talking about economic growth, the strategic context is more important than any one-off or short-lived factors. In this regard, looking strategically and with the long-term perspective a central bank should have, we expect that the asset quality review and stress test would have a positive impact on lending and hence on economic growth. Title: Interview, 24 Hours daily
Subtitle:
THERE WILL BE A DATE FOR THE EURO AREA WHEN 
WE ARE COMPLETELY READY
text: Interview with the BNB Governor Mr. Dimitar Radev on pages 13 and 14 of 24 Hours daily, 19 September 2016 THERE WILL BE A DATE FOR THE EURO AREA WHEN WE ARE COMPLETELY READY Markets, credit rating agencies and professional analysts confirmed the assessment of the banks assets and stress tests. More highlights: We are working on obtaining a license for printing euro banknotes in Bulgaria, which is not only a question of reputation but also of economic benefits. I see no threats to the Lev. Foreign exchange reserves are at historically high levels and are managed soundly and well. Mr Radev, what was the past year for the central bank and the banking system  hard, under slight pressure, or a routine one? I am asking because you took the helm of the BNB after the fall in public confidence in it and in banks. It was a difficult, but also a productive year. Generally our banking system now is in a better position both in terms of credibility and financial performance. At the time of your election you announced three types of measures  immediate, strategic and institutional. What is done on them and what is to come? We adhere strictly to the implementation of these measures. Our last year priorities were mainly related to improving banking supervision, developing the institutional framework for resolution of problems in the banking sector, and conducting an independent assessment of the position of the banking sector. Progress in all three areas is significant, but a lot of work is yet to be done, including in relation to the regulatory framework and operationalizing the banking sector recovery and resolution framework. The banking supervision reform was a priority for you  can we be certain that banking supervision will not sleep through the conception and proliferation of another KTB? We have reorganized significantly the banking sector in terms of both governance model and structure, and enhanced its capacity. The direct commitment of banking supervision to the recently completed asset quality review of banks assets and the very detailed information obtained about the position of individual credit institutions helped us to establish a very high standard of bank monitoring, to which we will adhere in the future, and to streamline the whole supervisory process. We already have at our disposal reliable mechanisms for resolution of problems in the banking sector. Therefore, as an institution we are much better prepared to face any potential challenges. We have heard your assessment of the stress tests and the assets. However, we have also heard voices that the situation differed from the officially announced one. Is such a manipulation in front of the eyes of the European Banking Authority, the ECB and the independent auditors possible? The results are what they are. They were established and summed up by highly reputed international audit companies. The assessments of this exercise by markets, credit rating agencies, and professional analysts were clearly positive. This assessment was also confirmed by the recently issued IMF statement. I have no problem with the fact that there are individual critical voices. Ultimately, it is all about the objectivity, professional arguments and good faith of the commentators, and the publics trust in them. What is your forecast of the interest rates, lending and deposits in a longer term horizon and after the cleansing diet of banks as a result of the tests? I expect an increased pace of lending but, as I have pointed out many times, that should not be an end in itself. In their lending banks should also adequately take account of and manage the risk they assume. The growing of household deposits in the banks over the recent years is a process which continues. The interest rates however are becoming an increasingly important factor for the concrete pace of this growth. As to the dynamics of interest rates and lending, it will continue to be conditioned by a set of factors, including the state and prospects of the business environment and the confidence of companies and households which would translate into higher demand for borrowed funds. The interest rates on deposits in the foreseeable future will remain under the influence of the high liquidity in the banking system. The direction of the interest cycle and monetary conditions in the euro area will also have an important bearing. A year ago you announced that the issue with our joining the European banking mechanism and the euro area would come to the agenda after the stress tests. If I ask you today when will that happen, what would your reply be? This issue has never been off the agenda. It requires a well-informed discussion and plenty of consultations. The central bank participates actively in the Coordination Council for Bulgarias preparation for euro area membership, which is chaired by the finance minister; however the date will be determined at the end, not at the beginning of the process. The comprehensive assessment of the banking system assets was one major step. The budget consolidation is also running at a faster-than-envisaged pace. As a state we should focus now on the structural reforms, which would allow faster growth of productivity and would bring incomes closer to the average European levels. Do you expect the announcement of a date to rekindle the debates about the overvalued or undervalued Lev? Does all this talking pose any threats? I dont think such discussions are relevant at this moment. A date will be announced when we and our partners are ready to do it. I see no threat to the Lev as long as the Ministry of Finance and the BNB play their proper roles and are doing what they should be doing, as the case is. Foreign exchange reserves are at historically high levels and are managed in the best and most secure way possible in spite of the tough conditions and volatility of international markets. A financial stability review is coming up. How is it going to end? The real part of the review will begin in early October and will be completed at the end of January 2017. The results are going to be announced in May next year after having been approved by the management bodies of the two institutions. The burden of the review, as regards the banking sector, will fall primarily on the BNB. The banks involvement in this process will be insignificant compared to the work they did during the completed assets quality review and stress test. A couple of days ago the National Audit Office made public the results from the annual audit of the BNBs budget. It found violations in public procurement procedures. Your comments, please? I must point out that the National Audit Office has no objections whatsoever with regard to the management of the BNBs budget over the last year. The findings regarding public procurement procedures refer to contracts from past years, some of which even go back to the year 2001 and had not been found before. Since the end of last year we have had a new General Secretary, and from the beginning of this year  a new Public Procurement Director. The two of them have been working on that issue and significant progress has been made in removing the violations. What will be your priorities during your second year in office? We are working on very specific tasks. The joint venture of the BNB Printing Works and the French company Oberthur Fiduciaire is seeking to obtain a license for production of euro banknotes. This will be not only a matter of reputation, but of economic benefits for Bulgaria too. A new cash centre is going to be built in Plovdiv, and it will meet the highest international standards. From a strategic perspective, there are three priorities: first, further integration of our country into Europes financial infrastructure; second, consolidation in the banking sector; and, third, strengthening of the BNBs institutional development, with a focus on two areas of critical importance  human resource management and IT management. Title: Interview on the show "This Morning" on BTV with Anton Hekimyan
text: Interview of the Manager of the BNB Mr. Dimitar Radev on the show "This Morning" on BTV with Anton Hekimyan, 30 September 2016. "This Morning" continues from the office of the governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, a man who very rarely gives interviews, but who has a heavy responsibility to keep the vault of Bulgaria. Dimitar Radev. Good morning! How are you doing? Thanks tobree. A little more than a year in the armchair of a bnb manager. Is the armchair comfortable? If I was looking for comfort, I wouldn't have chosen this armchair. Still, after a year you must be feeling a little better than when you had to pull out the hotcard offies as a legacy of Ivan Iskrov's reign. The last year has really been tense d0 a lot of tasks, short deadlines. You know that I presented an 18-month reform programme in my choice. We have concrete results from the implementation of this program. Banking supervision is in much better conditioning d0 both as a model of governance and as an organisation. We have an institutional framework in place to solve problems in the banking sector, something that was missing a year ago. Just less than 40 days ago, wereviewed the asset quality and stress test of the banks. Would you give this definition, which I gave d0 the pulling of hot potatoes from the previous management of the previous BNB manager? The legacy was as we found it onJuly 15th (2015- 2015). However, there wasalso a lot of mistrust in the BNB as an institution after what happened around the KTB case. Quite naturally, after the shock in 2014, there was a problem with the trust in the BNB and our entire banking system. All indicators in both the Central Bank and the entirebank and analysts show that we are on track to restore that trust. Do you think that everything about the KTB case is going to happen, or at least it will be forgotten? There is a process that is established in the law, has competent institutions. I am convinced that they will do the job as required by law. With regard to the Central Bank, we have drawn very serious conclusions. Many of the things we included in this 18-month reform plan stemmed precisely from the crisis in 2014 and we have identified precisely the areas in which the Central Bank should act d0 these were three main areas and we are implementing concrete measures. Is it possible that at the very moment we are talking, new, other processes are underway that are similar to those in KTB? What we did with theasset quality review was to give a comprehensive and independent assessment of our banking sector. In fact, the main focus was on what we say is an asset quality review. The stress test is a routine measure thatuses the results of the asset quality review to assess how resilient our banks will be under certain macroeconomic developments, including adverse macroeconomic developments. I use stress tests assomething by which a choir recognizes what happened in the banking sector, that banks were put in very drastic conditions, about whether they will actually deal with unemployment, with non-return of loans, really very difficult economic conditions. We don't color the results. The results were identified and summarized by independent external auditors. They have shown that our system is stable. For this there is one important indicator d0 the ratio between common equity and risk-weighted assets of banks. The review showed that this indicator amounts to 18.9% at an internationally recognised regulatory minimum of 4.5%. as well as international organisations. The International Monetary Fund also issued a press release on this topic and the assessment there was also a layingone. However, we journalists are sometimes more likely to color the results or evaluate them. We are talking about whether they are colored pink or not, but two banks appeared that did not show good results, one of them much larger. All banks are above this minimum regulatory threshold that is required so that no more drastic measures are taken. So there is no bank below the regulatory minimum. Of course, the results above this regulatory minimum vary between banks and this determines the measures that the Central Bank has prescribed for each bank. For the majority of banks, these measures include maintaining the current level of capital adequacy. we are talking about three banks, not two, one has already complied with the requirements in the framework of the review itself and the other two have to do so by the middle of next year. They have conditions set by the BNB. However, is it possible that they have presented their results in such a way that everything really seems within normal or that a very small buffer is needed. The central bank was required to manage and coordinate the activities of over900 experts, including representatives of the most prestigious international audit companies. it was also an important indicator for potential investors. And yet for one of the banks I spoke to, the smaller one, i will not mention names, it was found that it would be difficult to withstand even the rates that you predict, at which the circumstances in Bulgariawould normally develop d0 because it would struggle in the coming years. It is one of two different things. One is the asset review, which was to show whether we have banks that fall below the regulatory minimum. All banks are above this regulatory minimum. The second part of the exercise was to put banks in a hypothetical situation of a very serious banking and not only banking, but also an economic crisis that is unlikely, but we want to be fully prepared for any challenges. Depending on the results of the stress test, there are clearly banks that need to take steps to be ready to meet these challenges. In the field of hypotheses, of course, information has also emerged that in previous years, not during your term of office now, bnb reports have been withheld, which are related tothe stableness of certain banks. These are probably publications related to previous banking supervision reports. These reports are not, in principle, public documents by law, but I think these are reports from 4-5 years ago and more. These reports cannot in any way explain the state of play in the systemin 2016. The question is whether, then, even in the past, the necessary, adequate action measures have been taken to prevent specific meltdowns. Specifically on these reports, we responded. As I said, by law they are not public documents. Secondly, we have given information, we have done, of course, a full analysis. For one particular report for which we received an inquiry, we said that the measures that were recorded there were partially implemented, but then there are follow-up measures. We also gave information about what we have been doing since 2015. So I think there is no drama or conspiracy here. The stress tests are over, the banks are checked. However, what we call an upcoming financial stability review is imminent. What is this? This is a standard tool for diagnosing the financial system as a whole and how regulators are performing their functions. This review will start next week and continue until the end of January. The main commitment here is to the regulators d0 to the BNB and the FSC, as not only banks but also non-bank financial institutions are checked. critical, on which I rely, on whether the Central Bank is performing its functions, whether what we have done in the supervisory system is sufficient, or whether more needs to be done. This means that you will now be under a magnifying glass, GNI B, whether you are dealing with your duties, but also whether other state institutions onwhich stability depends? Naturally. The Ministry of Finance is also a leading institution in this review. The central bank will be the focus of attention when it comes to the banking sector. Is this going to cost us money? Not. When the inspection passes, when it is finished, for Bulgaria what will it mean? What if the resolution underneath isa 100-year-old? That's going to mean a lot. It will mean a factual assessment of what, especially if we are talking about the Central Bank, we have done within this 18-month plan. As I said, one of the highlights of this review will be our banking supervision, how to deal with the system as a whole. Whether this system poses risks to the country in regional terms. It will also assess what is tobe done from now on. critical and objective assessment. You mentioned that the Finance Minister also said that he, as well, would be checked precisely on this line. How's he doing? The data show that fiscal consolidation is proceeding at a faster pace than expected. I think it would really be avery serious achievement if this year's budget is broadly balanced and that has to do with all this issue of financial stability and how the country looks outward. How do you work with The Cabinet Borisov 2? That's very good. In fact, our main cont agent is the Ministry of Finance. Coordination at this stage is excellent, and as Isaid, we welcome: the better the budget is managed, this is something that the Central Bank maintains. Are there any tips that, for example, want you? It was from theFinance Ministry, Vladislav Goranov? We talk very often on a wide range of issues, as there are many touches. As you know, the Central Bank is a fiscal agent of the state under contract with the government. So there are a lot of topics we talkabout and these discussions are useful for both sides. One of the guarantors of security, for the stability of the lev. Is the Bulgarian currency stable now? The stability of the bgn is a function of the stability of the currency board. To date, the reserves are 45.3 billion, this means 180% coverage of BGN, which in turn meansthat both the foreign exchange board and the lev are stable. Are we already talking more actively about entering the euro area? Or is that still out there, at the other end of the table? A lot of work is being made on this topic at technical level. I think it's too early topublicly announce dates or measures, but there are very active consultations going on at technical level. The central bank is a very active participant in the Coordination Council on the country's accession to the euro area. So this is a topic that is on the agenda, especiallywith the ega after the asset review, since we also have the financial stability assessment. Because there's a difference between talking early and staying on the agenda. When he's on the agenda, maybe we're closer? You know that public speaking is usually very productive and we have one, including our own experience. It is good to have these technical consultations first and ultimately a political decision will be made. since it depends on both sides, and I think neither our country nor our partners are ready for such public speaking. Because people's main concerns are about whether they will become further impoverished if the euro is introduced in Bulgaria. Will something like this happen? Not. They should not have any concerns about this topic. It was about the currency board d0 next year it will be 20 years since its introduction. For these 20 years, we have always had stability and it will not change if we introduce the euro. If we are off the currency board, are we safe and stable enough to maintain a level to maintain our financial stability? We do not plan to leave the currency board, the only way out is the adoption of the euro. Are we going to getpoorer then? No. Categorically. Now do you think the Bulgarian is poor or rich? If we use the World Bank classification, Bulgaria is a country with above-average incomes. But of course, our criterion is the European Union, and we all know that we need to do much more, both in terms of productivityand in terms of income. Has Brexit affected our economy and our financial system in any way? In fact, Brexit hasn't happened yet. But the markets reacted immediately... The markets reacted after the referendum d0 there were shocks, there was volatility, but it was a cow. The markets havenow calmed down. It is very important how the process will proceed from here on out. the effects of Brexit on Bulgaria are minimal. Of course, in the long run there will be effects, but we will monitor how the process will develop. The effects of listening to your intonation are more like a minus sign on the front. Would they have a negative impact? In general, there are expectations. Every time there is uncertainty, the effects are negative, but the gloomy expectations for the short-term effects after the referendum have been refuted. Was there a reaction in the markets and does it still feel like this after the events that took place in Turkey this summer? Naturally. Especially for us, it's a potential risk. We are not looking at the issue from a political point of view, but in terms of the impact on our economy. We are closely monitoring all risks. Obviously, when there are problems with our neighbours, there are risks to the country. We try to assess these risks and this assessment iscontained in our macroeconomicand forecasts. And they are? That this could have a negative impact? Can. Naturally. What is to come in the next year for Dimitar Radev? The next year is about to continue what we started last year. Our main priorities are three. The first priority is integration into European financial infrastructure, which is relevant to the issue you have asked for the euro area. The second main priority is consolidation in the banking sector. We will see news in this area and they will be the result of what we have done in the asset quality review and the stress test. Consolidation this means a merger of banks, more, fewer players, a change in the system? Yes, it means every one of these things. It means more interest from strategic investors from outside. This interest was somewhere around zero a year ago, now we have such interest. What does this mean that foreign investors will buy banks that are currently on the territory of Bulgaria? Nothing specific, of course, we can't talk about. But I expect there to be news in the coming months on this topic. What would a merger of banks mean by your forecast? Banking consolidation is a topic not only for Bulgaria, but also for Europe. Melting interest margins put a lot of pressure on banks' profitability, forcing them to cut costs and streamline activity. This is a process we are seeing everywherein Europe. Our banks are not isolated. As a result of this pressure, one of the answers is consolidation. When wetalk about risks, interest inclusive, what happens to interest rates in Bulgaria? You know that there are countries that are looking at this option, there are countries that have introduced negative interestrates. Still? Still. Both loans and deposits. As I said, this puts a lot of pressure on banks, but on the other hand it gives better lending opportunities and households. What happens to the Bulgarian debt? Bulgaria stands very well as a level of debt relative to GDP. Bulgaria has the third lowest amount of debt relative to GDP (in the EU) after Eustonand Luxembourg. Will we have to take out more loans next year? To cover someone else's mistake, for example? This is a question for the Minister of Finance. But he made a very clear statement that at this stage such plans do not exist. And this has a very direct relation to the asset quality review. You probably know that the Ministry of Finance was planning, this was set in the budget, about BGN 2 billion in costs related to problem solving in the banking sector. The review showed that no such resource needs to be used. I say a mistake not by accident, because many people define so, and politicians including, Belene PP, the project, which is not yet clear whether it will take place or not, and there we will give a lot of money. It's a saga that's going on. The government has a clear plan for how to get out of this situation. But only 20-30 m from the BNB is located Dondukov 2. Are you following the saga of the presidential election and the upcoming campaign? Of course, as a voter, I follow them. Are you going to vote? Naturally. How do you like it so far? Is there a battle and will there be in the next month? It's normal to expect a fight. We see what's going on in the U.S. I think there will be enough emotion in our presidential election. You're frugal. Should the BNB governor stay out of politics? Absolutely. But if I ask you about America, you're sure to say how it's going to affect Bulgaria if it's Trump, and how would it affect if it was Hillary Clinton? So far, I'm just an observer. When things happen, then we'il make an assessment. Yet did the risks of one and the other judge them? These types of risks are far from us. There will be, of course, global development and economics, but these are things we will judge when they happen. How many hours do you spend in this office? How long have you been here? Different. I don't keep accurate statistics - 10-12 hours. A year ago, we met again here, around the banker's holiday. Then you told me you didn't bring anything here by yourself. Do you have one now? Basically not. I have additional books that bring me acquaintances, books that they issue. I am now looking at something that a colleague brought me some time ago d0 again, the problem is money, banks, credit. Thank you for this interview. Thanks to. Title: Interview, Banker weekly
Subtitle:
WE ARE DEVELOPING A COMPREHENSIVE SYSTEM OF CRISIS
MANAGEMENT AND PROVISION OF LIQUIDITY SUPPORT
text: Interview with the BNB Governor Dimitar Radev on p. 7, Banker weekly, 9 June 2017 WE ARE DEVELOPING A COMPREHENSIVE SYSTEM OF CRISIS MANAGEMENT AND PROVISION OF LIQUIDITY SUPPORT The euro area is a strategic goal for Bulgaria Mr. Radev, Bulgarias accession to the euro area has recently become a central subject in the political life in the country. To what extent is this goal realistic and attainable for Bulgaria presently? The euro area membership is a strategic goal but also an obligation for the country according to the EU accession treaty. To attain this goal, however, a number of conditions should be met, and thats exactly what we should focus our efforts on. Work on these conditions is important and useful for the country even outside the direct context of euro area membership. Ultimately, we should make a serious progress on a broad scope of subjects related to the countrys real convergence. Achieving such progress requires considerable efforts, but it is a real and attainable goal. What is BNBs role in Bulgarias joint efforts to attain this strategic goal  joining the euro area? The main role of the Central Bank is to implement strictly its mandate  maintaining the price stability and the stability of the currency board. This is what we are doing, and I believe we are doing it well. Of course, we are working on a number of concrete tasks related to the conditions that should be met in the banking sector, such as strengthening the banking supervision and developing the crisis management framework for the banking sector. On operational level, we are working in close coordination with the Ministry of Finance and our role in this process is clear  providing expert support. At the beginning of this year we prepared an extensive report on the costs and benefits of joining the euro area from the perspective of our tasks and expertise, which was submitted to the Euro Area Accession Coordination Committee. Naturally, joining the euro area is a complex matter including a number of tasks outside the mandate and activities of the Central Bank. What necessitated the review under the Financial Sector Assessment Programme (FSAP) and what are the benefits from it? The review of the condition of the financial sector, made by the IMF and the World Bank experts, was completed at the end of May. It provided the objective external assessment of what has been done and of what remains to be done. This assessment coincides with our own assessment. It clearly indicated that the banking sector in Bulgaria is stabilized after the problems we faced in 2014, as a result of the reforms implemented and the high capital and liquidity buffers of the system. A progress is also reported on the priorities we have had in the recent two years  priorities in accordance with the measures discussed with the EC. We are talking about the asset quality review of our banks, the improvement in supervision and the creation of the institutional framework for problem resolution in the banking sector  something we did not have in 2014 which then led to a number of problems. The IMF places an emphasis on the need to create an operating system for bank recovery and resolution. What are BNBs challenges in this area? The IMF also noted this system is already built on strong foundations. Our main focus now is to make it fully operational. There are two priorities. One of which is the resolution plans of our banks. We have already approved the resolution plans of the subsidiaries of the European banks. Now we are working on the resolution plans of domestically owned banks. This will happen by the year end based on clear criteria and methodology. One of the FSAP recommendations is for the BNB and the Ministry of Finance to establish a system of coordinated activities for provision of liquidity support to banks in full compliance with the currency board requirements. What measures are pursued to this effect? This is the second priority subject. Actually it is as old as the currency board. In 1997 we created the so-called Fiscal Reserve Account, aimed, inter alia, at providing resources for such liquidity support, as under a currency board regime the BNBs possibilities to do so are highly limited. This mechanism was used twice in the recent 20 years. Presently  under the EU directive for recovery and resolution of credit institutions and investment firms and the new rules for provision of government support, the old mechanism is inapplicable. The Ministry of Finance and the BNB are the two institutions that are most familiar with these matters and know what has to be done. Together with Minister Goranov we formed a joint team, who will quickly prepare a concrete proposal. Are there clear potential financial crises management arrangements in place now and what are the principles of their operation? As I said, the FSAP Report concludes that we have created sound foundations for this. These foundations include four key elements. First, the Financial Stability Advisory Council which comprises the Minister of Finance, the BNB Governor and the Chair of the Financial Supervision Commission. This Council meets regularly and there we discuss and coordinate our activities regarding a wide range of financial stability issues. The second key element is the Central Bank itself, which by law is designated to be the resolution authority for credit institutions. For this purpose we have already set up a special directorate which operates successfully. The third element is the mechanism to fund resolution measures through the established Bank Resolution Fund where the contributions of the banks in Bulgaria are collected. The resources collected into the Fund so far amount to nearly BGN 300 million, and the total amount required will be collected by 2024. And the fourth element is the full range of resolution tools, including sale of business, bridge institution, separation of assets, and loss-sharing. We have already made the two tasks in question a priority: the resolution plans and the liquidity support. Both the FSAP Report and the European Commissions latest recommendations to Bulgaria focus on the non-performing loans problem. What is the situation with the NPLs now? We are addressing this issue, and we have done so for some time now. As a result the portion of non-performing loans is still going down; now it is 12.6% from 14.6% at the end of 2015. This is yet above the EU average. Therefore, we will continue to create appropriate conditions for reducing non-performing loans, including by regulatory measures and guidelines for increasing loan loss provisions, higher NPL write-offs, by encouraging more conservative loan and collateral valuations, and also by further development of the secondary market. I should note that it is very important not only how we are handling the legacy of non-performing loans but also how to avoid the accumulation of new non-performing loans, especially in an environment where lending is starting to recover and where sooner or later interest rates would begin to rise. This requires more vigilant credit risk management in banks. Dont you think that this higher level of non-performing loans in Bulgaria in the total loan portfolio, which is twice as high as the average EU level, should raise serious concerns? This issue calls for a comprehensive assessment. Despite their high level, non-performing loans in Bulgaria are relatively well covered with provisions and capital. For example, the level of non-performing loan provisions in Bulgaria now is 53%, well above the EU average which is about 40%. Moreover, this sector has a capital surplus available which now is over BGN 7 billion, while the net value of non-performing loans is under BGN 5 billion. Therefore the in-depth analysis indicates that the problem is not so acute, but nevertheless it is an issue that we are working on very seriously. The FSAP Report recommends strengthening the measures against lending to related parties. What policies are planned in this area? Lending to related parties was checked during the asset quality review, but this topic is still high on our list of priorities so as to remove any open issues. For this purpose we are considering various options for changes to the legal framework, including amendments to laws, if needed, which would make the definition of related parties more precise and would provide additional supervisory tools for analysis. Our final decisions will also take into consideration the changes in the European Banking Authoritys guidelines on related parties, which are being adopted now. Given the banking situation in Bulgaria as outlined above, could we expect any growth in lending? What we see after the conducted asset quality review is a gradual recovery of lending, something that we expected to take place. In April this year credit growth for the private sector was 4.3% on an annual basis, while last April it decreased by 1.6%. The growth is still moderate but I expect this process to accelerate. This will be an important factor for the economic growth.

Title: Publication in the Quarterly Bulletin of the Association of Banks in Bulgaria
Subtitle:
THE BULGARIAN NATIONAL BANK BETWEEN 
THE ASSET QUALITY REVIEW AND THE EURO AREA
text: Publication of Mr. Dimitar Radev, BNB Governor, in the Quarterly Bulletin of the Association of Banks in Bulgaria, issue 48, January 2017 THE BULGARIAN NATIONAL BANK BETWEEN THE ASSET QUALITY REVIEW AND THE EURO AREA The implementation of the 18-month Plan on reforms and institutional development of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) that was completed at the end of 2016 had a highly disciplining effect on the banking sector in Bulgaria. Let me remind you that in addition to the Asset Quality Review (AQR) and the stress test of all commercial banks the Plan also envisaged immediate measures in two other priority areas: strengthening banking supervision and establishing an institutional framework for recovery and resolution of banks. The specific results from the successful implementation of the plan, in addition to the other factors, so far have been three: First, we evidence a process of recovery of lending. The growth of lending to the non-government sector started to move more confidently into positive territory. Second, the financial indicators in the banking sector improved significantly, as the overall profit for 2016 recovered near to the highest levels prior to the global crisis. Third, we see a strong impetus to market consolidation in the sector, as demonstrated by the recently announced deal between KBC and the National Bank of Greece for the acquisition of United Bulgarian Bank AD. Our banking system as a whole is in a better condition today than in 2015, which is of great positive significance both for the business, and for the economic growth prospects. However, banks should overcome certain ongoing challenges in relation to the internal and external political uncertainty, market volatility, decreasing interest margins and the need of sustained efforts to enhance the banking sector efficiency. Besides, banks are in the process of implementation of the measures prescribed by the BNB after the AQR and the stress test. Given these challenges, presently the work of the central bank is channelled in two directions: to continue along the line of discipline and reforms in the sector, which is productive as clearly demonstrated by the recent 18 months; and to carefully monitor external risks to the banking system and be ready to respond, if required. In terms of responding to external risks to the banking system, we have both the positive experience from the financial crisis in Greece, and the appropriate set of safeguards, which we can trigger if needed, including: imposing liquidity and/or capital requirements to foreign bank subsidiaries and branches; measures for attaining their operational independence within Bulgaria and for their independent liquidity management; as well as limiting their exposures to entities belonging to the same group. At the same time, all BNB actions are pursued in a long-term strategic context, namely  the strong commitment to continue the integration into the European institutional and financial infrastructure. For example, the reforms in the area of banking supervision, the establishment of an institutional framework for bank recovery and resolution, and organizing the AQR and stress test in the banking sector were an important precondition for considering our agenda through the prism of Bulgarias accession to the euro area. In view of what has been done so far, that agenda of the BNB contains three major groups of tasks: First, maintaining price stability by ensuring the stability of the national currency or, in other words, maintaining our monetary regime. At the end of 2016 the international foreign exchange reserves reached nearly BGN 47 billion, thus providing for over 160% coverage of the banknotes and coins in circulation, and of the liabilities to banks on the Issue Departments balance sheet. Second, developing a financial infrastructure which would fully correspond to euro area standards. That covers a wide range of issues, including payment systems maintenance and oversight, the relevant regulatory framework, information support and statistics. These are areas where we have either achieved or are close to achieving the highest international standards. Thus, for instance, our payment systems practically stand completely ready to meet the requirements in the event of acceding to the euro area. Another example, last year with the efforts of the BNB, the Ministry of Finance and the National Statistical Institute our country adhered to the highest global statistical standard used for financial stability purposes, the so-called SDDS plus. Bulgaria was among the first eleven countries to adhere to that standard along with a few leading European countries, the USA, and Japan. Third, continuing the reforms related to the banking sector. In the recent 18 months we have achieved a great deal in the supervision area, including with regard to the governance model, organizational enhancement and practical functioning of the supervisory activities. More tasks, however, remain to be completed. Thus, for instance, there will be amendments to the internal rules and procedures and the project for a new information system will start up, which would further enhance the compliance of our supervisory practices with the Basel Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision. Another important aspect of the continuing reforms is to bring into full-fledged operation the already set-up bank recovery and resolution system. These three groups of tasks largely coincide with the central banks agenda for integration into the European financial infrastructure. As a result of its implementation, we expect that in 2018 the banking sector and banking supervision would no longer be an open issue on the path to the euro area. That is a mandatory, yet not sufficient condition for membership. It would ultimately depend on the progress in other areas outside the BNBs mandate, which concern the structural reforms and the overall process of real convergence, as well as the political situation, both internally and externally. ____________ A summary of the statement of 11th Annual Meeting of Business with the Government, Sofia, 2017.

Title: Publication in Views The EUROFI Magazine. The magazine were disseminated during The Eurofi High Level Seminar 2017 before ECOFIN in Malta
Subtitle:
ADDRESSING UNDERLYING ISSUES OF
CROSS-BORDER INVESTMENT IN THE EU
text: A publication of the BNB Governor, Mr. Dimitar Radev in Views The EUROFI Magazine. The magazine were disseminated during The Eurofi High Level Seminar 2017 before ECOFIN in Malta, 5-7 April 2017 ADDRESSING UNDERLYING ISSUES OF CROSS-BORDER INVESTMENT IN THE EU We are witnessing a downward shift in cross-border investment in the EU, while the EU current account moved to positive territory in recent years. The savings-investment mismatches, therefore, are at the heart of the conundrum we face in developing the cross-border investment in the EU. Several initiatives to address this issue have been launched, including the Investment Plan for Europe, and the European Long-term Investment Fund. A large-scale new initiative is the establishment of the Capital Markets Union intended to further enhance the mobilization of capital and its channeling to companies and infrastructure projects offering new opportunities for savers and investors across the EU. A few other initiatives are under consideration, including the creation of a European Savings Investment Fund. However, the results of all initiatives have been mixed so far, and cross-border investment is stagnating. Before moving forward we need to better understand the underlying factors behind recent developments. The current initiatives look technically sound, but the lack of sufficient progress in their implementation reveals a number of remaining underlying issues. These include: (i) the unfinished agenda with regard to banking and financial integration; (ii) slow progress in real convergence; and (iii) limited availability of adequate infrastructure and innovation projects. Priority actions should, therefore, focus on addressing the underlying issues, and efforts at further expanding the already established toolkit come next. This would require bold steps at both the EU and national levels to regain confidence in the future of EU integration. At the EU level, there are institutional issues to be addressed concerning the future of the integration process. The five scenarios recently proposed by Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker shed light on the possible patterns of integration between the EU members. However, there remains a potential conflict between the prospects of multiple-speed developments and advancing real convergence between the euro area and the rest of the EU. The EU needs to move promptly on this issue, in order to address uncertainties. The national authorities, at their end, should promote financial stability and fiscal solvency, and address structural weaknesses and bottlenecks. The experience of Bulgaria may be indicative of what can be done by an EU member state that is not yet member of the euro area. From the central bank perspective this involves: (i) a sound banking sector; (ii) fiscal consolidation; and (iii) structural reforms. Good progress has been made in Bulgaria with regard to the first two areas. A comprehensive asset quality review in 2016 helped restore confidence in the banking sector. Bank lending is recovering, the overall profit is near historical highs and a process of market-based consolidation in the sector is underway, including a recent deal with a strategic investor from the euro area. Furthermore, the public finances of Bulgaria remain sound and the successful fiscal consolidation is illustrated by the budget surplus last year and the third lowest government debt to GDP ratio in the EU. As for the structural reform agenda, much more remains to be done in order to resolve remaining issues and help attract increased capital flows from the EU. We at the central bank have already planned the next steps, which will build on recent progress. Among other things, we plan to further strengthen our banking supervision, develop the crisis management framework for the banking sector, and reduce the level of nonperforming loans. To conclude, decisive actions are required at both the EU and national levels to address the current saving-investment mismatches within the EU. While expending the available toolkit is important, priority should be given to resolving the remaining underlying issues with regard to banking and financial integration, real convergence, and quality of project management.
