Title: Interview with Ms. Nina Stoyanova, Deputy Governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, Head of the Banking Department, on epicenter.bg, October 28, 2022
text: Interview by Ms. Nina Stoyanova, BNB Deputy Governor in charge of the Banking Department, for epicenter.bg, 28 October 2022 ADOPTION OF THE EURO WILL NOT INCREASE PRICES IN BULGARIA Bulgarias accession to the euro area is the next logical and necessary phase within the EU integration processes Ten seconds' transfers are now carried out by many banks in Bulgaria In a special interview given by the BNB Deputy Governor Nina Stoyanova for Epicenter.bg, she stated that any concerns about price rises were unfounded. The technical changeover of one legal tender to another at a fixed exchange rate, and by clear rules and conversion mechanism cannot in itself lead to pro-inflationary effects, affirmed Nina Stoyanova Highlights: - Bulgarias accession to the euro area is the next logical and necessary phase within the EU integration processes in which we are involved; - Authorisation of crypto-asset issuers and trading platforms will be introduced, oversight of their business by a public authority, and measures protecting clients funds; - One of the recently implemented projects that facilitate the preparations for the euro changeover is the migration of client credit transfers in BGN to the standards of the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), which also apply to the payments in the euro area. Interview: Ms. Stoyanova, to what degree the payment systems in Bulgaria are prepared for the adoption of the euro? Even now, the Bulgarian banks are able to make payments in euro both in the country and in Europe. This is possible thanks to the BNBs participation, since 2010, in TARGET2  the real-time gross settlement system in the euro area. Once the euro is introduced as the national currency, the BGN payments will begin to be executed as euro payments via the TARGET2-BNB national component system. In fulfilment of the HYPERLINK " " National Euro Changeover Plan of the Republic of Bulgaria, adopted in May 2022 by the Council of Ministers, the Payment Systems and Payment Service Providers Working Subgroup has been set up, and this group discusses and implements the activities required for adapting payment systems and for preparing the banking community for transition to payments in euro. Could the euro changeover and the related technical transformations have an impact on the level of prices in Bulgaria? The technical change of one legal tender with another at a fixed exchange rate, by clear rules and conversion mechanism cannot in itself lead to pro-inflationary effects. The ECB and Eurostat data on some of the countries that recently joined the euro area (Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia) show negligible inflation differences when the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) for the year of euro adoption is compared with the yearly average estimate for the preceding 12 months. For Slovenia, the calculated euro changeover-related effect on the annual inflation is also very small  around 0.2% - 0.3%. In this regard, any concerns that the adoption of the euro could give rise to a considerable inflation are unfounded and are rather caused by insufficient understanding and awareness. The argumentation that the euro changeover would not raise prices in Bulgaria was also supported in the recently published report by the Department of Economics within the Faculty of Economics and Business Administration in Sofia University. An important step in this direction, which also enhances the citizens greater awareness, is the concept of a Law on the Euro Changeover in the Republic of Bulgaria, published on 20 October this year by the Council of Ministers, and drawn up by an interdepartmental working group. This law will establish the principles, rules and procedures for the introduction of the euro as an official currency in Bulgaria. What are these procedures? Among them are the principle of converting Bulgarian levs into euros at a fixed exchange rate of BGN 1.95583 for EUR 1, a one-month period of dual circulation of the Bulgarian lev and the euro starting from the changeover date, free of charge physical exchange of Bulgarian banknotes and coins at the Bulgarian National Bank with no limit in time, and in commercial banks and Bulgarian Posts AD  free of charge in the first 6 months after the changeover, a period for dual display of prices  starting one month after the Council of the European Unions decision on Bulgaria's euro area accession and lasting for 12 months after the official introduction of the euro as legal tender in Bulgaria, etc. The law will guarantee the protection of consumers during the conversion of prices and the compliance with the principle that consumers would not be put at a more disadvantageous position than they would have been if the euro had not been introduced. It provides for the required control and sanctioning mechanisms to ensure that these rules are complied with. Bulgarias accession to the euro area is the next logical and necessary phase within the EU integration processes in which we are involved. I would like to remind you that in July 2020 the Bulgarian lev was included in the Exchange Rate Mechanism II (ERM II) at the current fixed exchange rate of the Bulgarian lev for euro. In October 2020 our country joined the Single Supervisory Mechanism (so-called Banking Union) and the Single Resolution Mechanism, and as a result today the Bulgarian banking sector practically operates by the rules applicable to the euro area. What type of digital services should we introduce in order to enter into the euro area? All digital services and channels available in Europe are also offered on our market. This is possible due to the many years of consistent efforts by the BNB, BORICA as payment systems operator and the banking community, all resulting in establishing a modern, secure and dynamically evolving infrastructure. One of the recently implemented projects that facilitate the preparations for the euro changeover is the migration of client credit transfers in BGN to the standards of the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), which also apply to the payments in the euro area. This project allows, from the beginning of this year, client credit transfers within the country to be executed within less than an hour from the time of initiating the payment order to the time of crediting the recipients account. Currently, we are working to implement a similar project for migration to the SEPA standards for public sector payments too, which would also improve their efficiency and execution time. Could we say now that our mobile phone can to some extent perform the functions of a digital bank? Indeed, nowadays the smartphone is increasingly becoming a tool for initiating payments as well as for executing many other electronic transactions. This is possible due to services, such as digitalisation of payment cards, the use of digital wallets and mobile banking applications, which are already widespread in our country. A new possibility is the transfer between accounts by referring to a mobile phone number instead of an account number, based on a technology that links the telephone number and the IBAN number. This service is now offered on the Bulgarian market too. Lately, there is ongoing work on the use of smartphones as a kind of software POS terminals capable of receiving payments with physical payment cards and payment instruments integrated in the mobile phone. In our country there are now payment service providers that offer this software POS service too. At what stage is the concept of instant transfers, that is to receive a transfer within a few seconds, how is this project progressing? The instant BGN payments project was launched last year and it is already operating in a live environment with clients. It allows the execution of transactions within 10 seconds, 365 days a year. Some of the biggest banks in the country are now involved in this project, and nearly 2/3 of the client accounts in Bulgaria are already accessible for instant payments. The deadline for migration to the new instant payments platform is April 2023. The successful completion of this project and the extensive participation of the banking community in it create preconditions for easier future migration to instant euro payments, in accordance with the standards applicable in the euro area. Are there any reasons for concern regarding the cryptocurrency transactions? The purchase of crypto-assets, also known as cryptocurrencies, is a type of investment that entails certain risks. The most significant risk related to these assets is that they are not currencies and are not legal tender, they are not backed by any public authority issuing them, and generally their value is not backed by any real or financial asset, which leads to great volatility of prices. For that reason, the European and national regulators have repeatedly published clarifications and warnings to consumers. It is important to note that the activities of issuing and trading in crypto-assets in Europe are going to become regulated. A comprehensive EU regulation on the markets in crypto-assets (MiCA) is expected to be adopted by the end of this year. It will introduce authorisation of crypto-asset issuers and trading platforms, regulation of their business by a public authority, and measures safeguarding clients funds. The MiCA regulation will ensure that issuer of a given crypto-asset will provide complete and understandable information about the functionalities and risks relating to the respective product. This will help consumers make decisions based on full and standardised information about the asset they intend to invest in. PAGE \* MERGEFORMAT 2

Title: Interview with Ms. Nina Stoyanova, Deputy Governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, Head of the Banking Department, on epicenter.bg, December 7, 2022
text: Interview of Ms Nina Stoyanova, BNB Deputy Governor in charge of the Banking Department, for epicenter.bg, 7 December 2022 THE LAW ON ADOPTION OF THE EURO WILL INCLUDE MEASURES AGAINST PRICE GROWTH The exchange of the lev for the single currency will be free How will payment systems change with the adoption of the euro? After the introduction of the euro in Bulgaria, all payment transactions in the country, which until then have been carried out in levs (BGN), will start to be executed in euros. According to the National Euro Changeover Plan of the Republic of Bulgaria, adopted in May 2022, payment system operators (including the BNB) and payment service providers in the country are committed to the preparation and implementation of the necessary changes in the payment infrastructure in our country. In terms of payments, perhaps the most tangible change will be the discontinuation of the real-time gross settlement system in BGN (RINGS), as it only processes BGN payments. All these payments, which until then have been processed by RINGS, will move to be processed and settled in the gross settlement system of the euro area TARGET2, which will also require some legislative changes in our country. The processes of migration to euro payments have actually been underway for quite some time now and many of the changes have already been implemented or are in the process of being implemented. Since 2010, the BNB has been operating a national component system in TARGET2. This allows the country's banking community to make euro transfers domestically and cross-border via TARGET2 even at present. This infrastructure is also complemented by the payment system for customer payments in euro BISERA7-EUR, operated by BORICA AD, which, through the connectivity built with other systems in Europe, enables the exchange of euro transfers with customers of banks from other European countries. In addition, at the beginning of this year, a project was implemented for the migration of customer credit transfers in BGN towards the standards of the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA). Thus, in practice, customer credit transfers in BGN already meet the technical and business requirements of the standards for credit transfers in the euro area and are executed in less than an hour. Another important project that is already working in live environment is for instant payments in BGN, where transactions are carried out within 10 seconds, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. The development of instant payments in BGN is also very important for the integration of national payments to the standards for instant payments in the euro area. These projects are implemented by BORICA AD with the participation of the Bulgarian banking community and with the assistance of the BNB. All these changes have led to a serious reduction in the execution time of customer credit transfers in the country, without this in itself leading to an increase in fees for payment transactions for end users. Changes are also coming regarding public sector payments, which should also migrate to SEPA standards. This is also included as an activity in the National Euro Changeover Plan of Bulgaria. The Ministry of Finance, BNB, BORICA AD and the banks in the country are currently working on this activity. All these changes, which have already been completed or are in the process of implementation, are prerequisite for an easier technical migration to payments in euros when the currency changeover takes place. Will changing the lev for the euro cost us customers anything after the adoption of the euro? According to the National Euro Changeover Plan and the draft Law on the introduction of the euro in Bulgaria (the so-called Euro Law), the conversion of the funds on accounts from levs to euros will be automatic and free of charge on the day of the introduction of the euro in Bulgaria. In addition, it is planned that the physical exchange of lev banknotes and coins for euros will be free of charge for the cash exchange service at banks and Bulgarian Posts PLC during the first six months of the introduction of the euro, and their exchange at the BNB will be free of charge without a deadline. A consumer protection principle will be enshrined in the Euro Law, which ensures that the conversion of prices and other values from BGN to EUR will not put consumers in a worse financial position than they would have been if the euro had not been introduced. Protection against possible abuses and unfair commercial practices, as well as effective monitoring and control tools to reduce the risk of price increases as a result of the introduction of the euro, are also foreseen. How will bank fees change after the country joins the euro area? As I have already indicated, the conversion of receivables and payables into euros and the transition to payments in euro is not expected to result in additional charges on customers after joining the euro area. The process of preparing the necessary changes and adjustments in the systems and processes in connection with the changeover to the euro has already begun in accordance with the National Euro Changeover Plan and is yielding positive results. In addition, the integration to the payment infrastructures and standards of the euro area will lead to more efficient and faster execution of payments within the country and toward other European countries, which in turn should optimise the costs of these services. In this respect, the introduction of the euro as a legal tender in Bulgaria would have indisputable advantages in the financial sphere. It is expected to lead to lower transaction costs for businesses and citizens, as well as to a more complete and comprehensive integration of national payment systems with the European ones. Title: Address by Ms. Nina Stoyanova, Deputy Governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, Head of the Banking Department, at the opening of a conference on "The Role of Organized Civil Society in the Process of Bulgaria's Accession to the Eurozone", organized by the Economic and Social Council of Bulgaria, 9 May 2023.
text: Speech by Ms. Nina Stoyanova, BNB Deputy Governor in charge of the Banking Department, at the opening of the SPOTLIGHT ON T2S workshop, 20 January 2023 Under the National Euro Changeover Plan of the Republic of Bulgaria, multiple measures and activities are well underway, involving changes in the payment and settlement systems. With regard to the securities settlement in Bulgaria, the main measure that is planned to take place is the onboarding of the BNBs Government Securities Depository (BNBGSSS) and the Central Securities Depository AD (CD AD) to the securities settlement platform TARGET2-Securities (T2S). TARGET2-Securities is one of the primary EU-wide market infrastructures designed and run by the Eurosystem. This platform plays a key role in creating a single securities market in Europe and, generally, in achieving greater integration of financial markets in the European Union. Currently 19 depositories from European countries use T2S, and once the depositories in our country have joined the platform, the Bulgarian securities will become more easily accessible to the investors in the European Union. The benefits of the T2S platform are beyond dispute  it offers pan-European settlement, settling cash and securities in central bank money. TARGET2-Securities provides harmonised and standardised settlement services by means of delivery versus payment (DvP), on a gross basis and in real time, and the transfer of money and securities is done on a state-of-the-art technical platform that operates by the latest standards. The platform offers a number of advantages to both securities issuers and securities investors, such as cross-border settlement, a diversified portfolio of investments, and a more diverse investor base. TARGET2-Securities will be integrated into the Eurosystems new consolidated platform for TARGET services, to which all the participants in the Bulgarian national component system (TARGET2-BNB)  the BNB, banks, payment systems, and securities settlement systems  are going to migrate in March 2023, together with the other central banks and participants in the platform. The new consolidated platform for TARGET services will, in terms of both technical and functional aspects, combine the TARGET2 payment system (in which the BNB participates since 2010 by operating a national component system), the TARGET2-Securities settlement platform (which the BNBGSSS is about to join, together with CD AD), the euro instant transfers service TIPS (to which an adherence is also planned in 2023), as well as the common Eurosystem Collateral Management System (ECMS) which is expected to go live in April 2024, with all euro area central banks participating in it. After that date, only securities in T2S will be used as collateral on the Eurosystems main refinancing operations, if they meet the relevant criteria. For this purpose, a link is envisaged between 2S and the new Eurosystem Collateral Management System, with the funds on these operations being settled on the accounts in the new consolidated platform for TARGET services. Once Bulgaria has joined the euro area, the specified functionalities will assist the BNB to fully perform the functions of a central bank of the Eurosystem. In view of the complexity and importance of the upcoming work on joining T2S, the preparation of the BNBGSSS and CD AD accession projects began already in 2021, with the two depositories once again realising a successful cooperation. To this end, teams from the BNB and CD AD were set up, which began work on preparation and familiarisation with the relevant technical documentation, jointly with experts from the European Central Bank (ECB). As a result of hard and intensive work, in 2022 BNBGSSS and CD AD prepared self-assessments of their systems and business processes, according to the Eurosystems requirements for joining T2S. In the fourth quarter of last year, CD AD and BNBGSSS successively signed Framework Agreements with the ECB for participation in T2S. In the current year 2023, the project enters a new phase, with tests and implementation to be carried out, for which the BNB is actively assisting as a central bank operating a national component system in TARGET2. In accordance with the Eurosystems schedule, the tests of the Bulgarian depositories for joining the platform start already in the first quarter of 2023, and tests with the participants of the depositories are planned to take place in the second quarter of this year. The goal is for Bulgarian depositories to join T2S within this year's migration window, currently planned for September 2023, when several more depositories from the EU are expected to join the platform. For the successful and timely implementation of the project, the BNB communicates on a regular basis with CD AD and the banks participating in BNBGSSS. In September 2022, an explanatory seminar was held with the BNBGSSS participant banks, which was of great benefit for the awareness and coordination with market participants. The current event is a natural continuation of this process. The good cooperation between the ECB, the BNB and CD AD, and the coordination with the market participants are important prerequisites for implementing the necessary changes in the relevant infrastructures and securities settlement systems in Bulgaria. The upcoming changes are a necessary and correct step that will help the securities depositories in our country to become part of the harmonised and integrated European financial market and payment infrastructure. ____________ Adopted by the Council of Ministers in May 2022 PAGE \* MERGEFORMAT 1

Title: Speech by Ms. Nina Stoyanova, Deputy Governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, Head of the Banking Department, at the opening of the SPOTLIGHT ON T2S seminar, January 20, 2023
text: Speech by Ms. Nina Stoyanova, BNB Deputy Governor in charge of the Banking Department, at the opening of the Fintech Hackathon From Zero to Fintech 2023, 18 March 2023 I would like to thank the Bulgarian Fintech Association and the Faculty of Economics and Business Administration at Sofia University for inviting me to take part in this Fintech Hackathon. It is a pleasure for me to open todays event, which favours financial education and enhances awareness of the latest tendencies in the Fintech sector. Innovations in payments area are developing at a rapid pace. The evolution of the hardware and software, coupled with a favourable regulatory framework, allowed the Fintech sector to flourish. The fast advancement of technology and adequate policies of regulators unleashed the private sector's creativity and ingenuity. The more convenient and accessible payment services have changed consumers attitude and preferences. We observe a highly competitive environment supporting the development of fast, secure and convenient digital channels for payments. According to a Study on payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (named SPACE), published by the European Central Bank in December 2022, in the euro area it was possible to pay with non-cash instruments in 81% of the transactions in 2022. According to the same study, cashless means of payments, particularly mobile phone apps, increased substantially in terms of P2P payments. Between 2019 and 2022, the share of mobile payments more than tripled in terms of number (from 3% to 10%), and more than doubled in terms of value (from 4% to 11%). Nowadays, we see how well the Fintech sector can cooperate with the traditional financial sector players as well as the public sector. Around the world, central banks are exploring how to give money new capabilities in the increasingly digitalising financial world of today. An important project for Europe, which we are closely following, is the work on the digital euro. Currently, the European Central Bank is going through an investigation phase, which is expected to be completed in the autumn of 2023. It explores technical and regulatory aspects of a digital euro. During this phase, the Eurosystem is actively collaborating with a wide range of stakeholders at an institutional level as well as with market participants. The Eurosystem is considering a digital euro app/ wallet with pan-European reach. Furthermore, the supervised entities would be able to integrate the digital euro in their own payment platforms. Another example for successful cooperation between Fintech, banks and public authorities is the open banking initiatives that are active across Europe. The Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) introduced two new regulated types of electronic payment services in the EU  payment initiation services and account information services. These new services form the basis of todays open banking. They enable Fintech companies to enter the payment market more easily and to introduce new and competitive business models and services. Examples for such services are aggregation of payment account data from different payment service providers, the opportunity to initiate payments from accounts held with different banks, collection of data for financial analysis purposes, etc. We already have national providers that successfully offer such services in Bulgaria. In order to meet the EU regulatory requirements regarding the open banking, Bulgarian banks, like the majority of the banks in Europe, have predominantly opted for the development of dedicated interfaces known as Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). These special interfaces ensure that providers of the new payment-related services have a secure and reliable access to the relevant banking systems. As a result, we are observing a developing cooperation between banks and Fintech companies. Open banking provides a basis for better, more integrated and secure services to the benefit of clients. The BNB is closely monitoring the processes and is supporting actively the Bulgarian market in order to reach the full potential of the open banking and to remove any potential obstacles in this respect. As a next step, the European Commission is planning to create a framework for data-sharing between companies in the financial sector. This more extended exchange of data is known as open finance. In short, open finance refers to third-party access to personal financial data. Open finance is broader in scope than open banking, as it covers not only payments but also banking, investment and insurance products. While open banking is already incorporated into financial market regulations, there is no legal framework yet that sets out the terms for the overall implementation of open finance. The European Commission is now seeking to change this with its Digital Finance Strategy for the EU. The purpose of such a new framework on open finance would be to enable, with the customers consent, financial service providers to share and reuse customers data, which fall outside the scope of PSD2. Thus, Fintech companies, banks and other financial sector companies could develop more convenient and cheaper products that are better tailored to customers needs. As I already said, a favourable environment for the development of payment services was created by the Second Payment Services Directive. Now PSD2 is in effect for more than five years. Time has come to assess the impact of its application in the EU and the need for potential amendments and adjustments. The review of PSD2 is expected to include an assessment of the impact of strong customer authentication on the level of payment frauds and a potential space for improvements. Further standardisation of dedicated interfaces used to facilitate the open banking activities is also included in the review of PSD2. In August 2022 ended the public consultation of the European Commission on the review of PSD2 and the gathering of information about a possible new open finance framework and the results are expected later this year. I would like to point out that the changes in the payments and financial sector of our country fully correspond to the European trends. Currently, an intensive work is in progress aiming to modernise further the payment infrastructure, including in the context of its future integration into the euro area infrastructures. In a few days, on 20 March 2023, the Bulgarian National Bank, banks and payment systems  participants in the Bulgarian national component system (TARGET2-BNB) of the TARGET2 system for large value payments in euro are joining the new consolidated TARGET Services platform. The platform combines on a technical and functional level the TARGET2 payment system, the securities settlement platform TARGET2-Securities (T2S) and the service for instant transfers in euro TIPS. The BNB and the Bulgarian banking community have been participating in TARGET2 since 2010 and they are aiming to join TARGET2-Securities and TIPS until the end of 2023. The new consolidated platform is expected to improve the overall efficiency and security of the existing systems and services. We share the view that the dialogue and cooperation with all stakeholders, including Fintech companies, are key to achieving our common goals and reaping to the full the benefits of the innovations in financial sector. I wish an interesting and fruitful work to all participants in the From Zero to Fintech 2023 event. PAGE \* MERGEFORMAT 2

text: Welcome speech by Ms. Nina Stoyanova, BNB Deputy Governor in charge of the Banking Department, at the opening of the conference The role of organised civil society in the process of Bulgaria's accession to the euro area, organised by the Economic and Social Council of Bulgaria, 9 May 2023 Dear Ms. Russinova, Dear colleagues and guests, On behalf of the Governor of the Bulgarian National Bank and on my behalf, I would like to welcome the participants in todays discussion and to thank the organisers from the Economic and Social Council for the invitation. The Economic and Social Council, with its strong and active stance on important issues relevant to the development of our country and as a representative body of a wide variety of civil society structures, is a particularly suitable host of todays event. Our society needs such discussions which professionally and openly debate on the single European currency, with the wide representation of national institutions, employers, trade unions, consumers, and guests from countries that have already introduced the euro and see the real effects of that on their economies and finances. According to the publicly available information from the European Central Bank (ECB), today the euro is the national currency of 20 countries out of all 27 member states of the European Union (EU) and of over 346 million European citizens. It is well-known that the last country to join the euro area was Croatia, as of 1 January 2023. The experience of Croatia and of the countries which preceded it (Estonia in 2011, Latvia  in 2014, and Lithuania  in 2015), representatives of which are participating in today discussion, is especially valuable to us. The ever-expanding territory of the single European currency enables full use of all the advantages of the single market in terms of lower transaction costs, a more integrated European economy, improving the opportunities for trading, investment and competition. The Bulgarian National Bank, jointly with the Ministry of Finance and the banking community in the country, is working actively, within its competences, to carry out the activities specified in the HYPERLINK " " National Euro Changeover Plan of the Republic of Bulgaria. The Bank is the leading institution in the Money, payment infrastructure and credit institutions working group organised to the Coordination Council for the Preparation of the Republic of Bulgaria for Euro Area Membership. Three sub-groups have been set up under this group, each one headed by a Deputy Governor of the BNB in the context of the activities that fall within its remit. Our experts are taking part in the preparation of the national legal framework relating to the introduction of the euro. The Law on the Introduction of the Euro in the Republic of Bulgaria, which is already prepared, constitutes the main legal act establishing the rules and procedures for the euro changeover in the country in accordance with the principles of transparency, awareness, and maximum protection of consumers. A working group at the Bulgarian National Bank has drawn up a draft of a new Law on the Bulgarian National Bank aiming to introduce all the necessary changes to the policies, activities and operations performed by the central bank, in compliance with the requirements of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, the Statute of the European Central Bank and the European System of Central Banks, and the other applicable legal acts. We are working in close cooperation and in very good communication with the European Central Bank on all technical issues related to changes in the systems and processes operated by the Bulgarian National Bank as a future participant in the Eurosystem  the system of central banks, which consists of the ECB and the national central banks of the member states whose official currency is the euro. Today, we will have the opportunity to debate over all aspects of the preparations for introduction of the euro in Bulgaria with representatives of the Bulgarian institutions and participants from countries that have already adopted the euro as their national currency and can share their impressions of how the process is running and its effects on their economies and institutions. I wish interesting and productive work to all the participants in the discussion! ____________ Adopted by the Council of Ministers in May 2022. PAGE \* MERGEFORMAT 2

Title: Speech by Ms. Nina Stoyanova, Deputy Governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, Head of the Banking Department, at the opening of the annual conference of Capital and Economedia Annual Fintech and Insurtech Summit, March 28, 2023
text: Statement by Ms. Nina Stoyanova, BNB Deputy Governor in charge of the Banking Department, at the conference The role of organised civil society in the process of Bulgaria's accession to the euro area, organised by the Economic and Social Council of Bulgaria, 9 May 2023 Dear Ms. Russinova, Dear colleagues and guests, I would like to thank the organisers from the Economic and Social Council for inviting me to take part in todays discussion. In this panel we are expected to discuss Bulgarias current progress on its way to euro area membership from the perspectives of various institutions that are involved in this process. I would like to focus on three topics  analysis of the requirements with regard to the legal framework, as set out in the convergence reports regularly issued by the ECB and the European Commission (EC), changes in the legal framework, and the technical preparations. Convergence reports of the ECB and the EC Under Article 140 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU, at least once every two years or at the request of a Member State with a derogation (an EU Member State that has not yet introduced the euro), the European Central Bank and the European Commission, separately, prepare reports for the Council of the EU, which assess the progress made by the Member States with a derogation in fulfilling their obligations regarding the achievements of the Economic and Monetary Union. The latest convergence reports of the ECB and of the EC were issued in June 2022. These 2022 convergence reports examined 7 countries which had not yet adopted the euro as their national currency but were committed to do so. The convergence reports of the ECB and the EC evaluate the fulfilment of the criteria for economic and legal convergence. In the legal domain, the reports review subjects related to the independence of national central banks in its four aspects: functional, institutional, personal and financial independence. They also examine the compliance with the prohibitions on monetary financing and privileged access of the public sector to financial institutions, the confidentiality requirements, etc. All these requirements need to be complied with by the relevant country upon its entry in the EU. As a result of amendments made to the Law on the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) and other national legal acts, it was achieved the required compliance; some remaining amendments in these areas are going to be adopted with the new draft Law on the BNB. Another part of the requirements that is examined and evaluated by the reports refers to the legal integration of the respective national central banks into the Eurosystem. That part of the reports reviews the compatibility with legal provisions regarding monetary policy, statistical data collection, official foreign reserve management, payment systems, issue of banknotes, appointment of independent auditors, financial reporting, international cooperation, etc. These requirements relate to the introduction of the euro as the national currency and are going to be met with the adoption of the new Law on the BNB. Changes in the national legal framework By order of the BNB Governor, a working group in the BNB has prepared a draft of a new Law on the BNB, which would fulfil all the requirements related to the introduction of the euro and the accession of the BNB to the Eurosystem. Since the changes are numerous and affect all areas of the bank's activities and almost all provisions of the law, the approach chosen was to draft a new law to replace the Law on the BNB of 1997, which introduced a currency board regime. The draft law is in the process of consultation with the ECB. According to the draft Law on the BNB, the currency of the Republic of Bulgaria is the euro divided into 100 cents. The law regulates the BNBs participation in defining and implementing the monetary policy of the Eurosystem in accordance with the provisions of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU, the Statute of the ESCB and the ECB and the applicable acts of the ECB. The law provides that, in accordance with the provisions of EU law, the BNB provides the ECB with foreign reserve assets up to an amount determined in accordance with Article 30 of the Statute of the ESCB and the ECB. The Bulgarian National Bank holds and manages its reserve assets that are not related to the monetary policy of the Eurosystem, in accordance with the provisions of EU law and the Law on the BNB. The new draft Law on the BNB, as far as possible and in accordance with the applicable European legal framework, preserves the governance structure and the functions hitherto performed by the central bank in the field of: exercising supervision over the activity of credit institutions, performing the function of a resolution authority, facilitating the establishment and functioning of efficient payment systems, regulation and supervision of the activity of payment systems operators, payment service providers and electronic money issuers, carrying out statistical and research activities, etc. It is envisaged the new Law on the BNB to enter into force on the date specified in the Decision of the Council of the EU on the adoption of the euro by the Republic of Bulgaria. Technical preparations Preparations for the adoption of the euro from an organisational and technical point of view are going according to the National Euro Changeover Plan of the Republic of Bulgaria. The Bulgarian National Bank is a leading institution in the Money, Payment Infrastructure and Credit Institutions Working Group. Within this group, three subgroups have been created, each headed by a BNB deputy governor within the scope of the activities falling within their specific areas of responsibility. The activity of the working subgroups is reported on a monthly basis with reports to the Coordination Council for the preparation of the Republic of Bulgaria for euro area membership and to the BNB Governing Council. In the area of adaptation of the payment systems for the introduction of the euro, which fall under the competences of Banking Department, we have been working on several parallel projects with a deadline for completion by the end of this year. First of all, this is the project for the migration of budget payments to the standards of the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA), which is expected to be completed in October 2023 and bring about a complete optimisation and acceleration of the process of banking service of the budget. The migration of customer credit transfers in BGN to the standards of the Single Euro Payments Area has now been completed, as a result of which customer credit transfers are executed in less than an hour, and instant credit transfers, which are already available for over 90% of customer accounts in the country, are executed within 10 seconds. By the end of 2023, the project to join the BISERA7-EUR payment system operated by BORICA AD to the Eurosystem service for the settlement of instant transfers in euro TIPS, is expected to be completed, which will allow banks in the country to also offer euro instant transfers. The Bulgarian National Bank and BORICA AD are working to ensure, by the end of 2023, full reachability in executing credit transfers in euro to over 4,800 payment service providers in all countries of the SEPA area, applying a prepaid model with continuous settlement, which will reduce the time for carrying out credit transfers in euro. We are working to join the Government Securities Depository in the BNB and Central Depository AD to the securities settlement platform TARGET2-Securities (T2S). This platform is one of the main pan-European market infrastructures developed and maintained by the Eurosystem. At the moment, 19 depositories from European countries use T2S, and several more depositories, including those from Bulgaria, are expected to join this year. Participation in the platform will contribute to better accessibility of Bulgarian securities for EU investors. In technical terms, we are already witnessing the beneficial and catalyst effect of the mentioned projects, which have been completed or are in the process of completion, on optimising the payment process and improving banking conditions in our country. In the field of payment and settlement systems, all projects related to the euro area accession will be completed by the end of 2023. ____________ Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Croatia, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Sweden. Of the EU Member States that have not yet adopted the euro, only Denmark, which has agreed not to participate in phase three of the Economic and Monetary Union and therefore has no obligation to adopt the euro as its national currency, is not assessed in the reports. In accordance with Art. 140, paragraph 2 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU and Regulation of the Council of the EU adopted in accordance with Art. 140, paragraph 3 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU. Title: Speech by Ms. Nina Stoyanova, Deputy Governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, Head of the Banking Department, at a conference on "The Role of Organized Civil Society in the Process of Bulgaria's Accession to the Eurozone", organized by the Economic and Social Council of Bulgaria, 9 May 2023.
text: Address by Ms. Nina Stoyanova, BNB Deputy Governor in charge of the Banking Department, at the jubilee 25th National Meeting of Municipal Financiers in the Republic of Bulgaria organised by the National Association of the Municipalities in Bulgaria, Golden Sands Resort, 29 May 2023 Dear Ms. Georgieva, Ladies and Gentlemen, First of all, I would like to thank the National Association of Municipalities for inviting me to take part in this years jubilee 25th National Meeting of Municipal Financiers in the Republic of Bulgaria and to congratulate the participants and the organisers of this meeting. I thank the organisers for bringing up the topic of the euro changeover, the responsibilities and preparations of the municipalities in this process, as one of the central issues to be debated at todays meeting. It is especially important for me to speak today on this subject before you, the financiers from the municipalities in the country because I highly value your expertise and experience, and I hope that the information on the various aspects of the preparations for euro adoption would reach, through you, every settlement in the country. The euro is one of the brightest symbols of the European identity and affiliation. It was launched on 1 January 1999, initially in an electronic form used for banking transactions, and from 1 January 2002 also in the form of banknotes and coins, which constitute the official currency of 12 countries. In the following years, also as a result of the enlargement of the European Union, eight more countries successively joined the euro area  Slovenia, Cyprus, Malta, Slovakia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, and most recently Croatia  as from 1 January 2023. The euro is the official currency of 346 million European citizens from 20 Member States of the European Union. Today the euro is the second most widely used currency in the world, after the US Dollar. The experience of each euro area country is important for us because it provides objective information on the process of euro adoption and the actual impact on the economy of the respective country. Recently, widely attended events have been often organised to discuss euro changeover-related issues, and representatives of the National Association of Municipalities have been active participants in them. The latest such event was a conference on the topic The role of organised civil society in the process of Bulgarias accession to the euro area held on 9th May this year. It was organised by the Economic and Social Council  a national consultative body that expresses the will of the civil society structures on issues of economic and social development. Tomorrow Sofia will host a similar forum organised by the Union for Private Economic Enterprise on the subject of Eurozone: Advantages and Challenges. These events are an important part of the objective, competent and professional discussion of all the issues related to the euro adoption that are of concern to our society. The Coordination Council for the preparation of the Republic of Bulgaria for euro area membership has adopted a Communication Strategy for Information and Publicity of Bulgaria's Accession to the Euro Area, published on the websites of the Ministry of Finance and the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB). The activities specified in the Strategy are to be implemented, and the municipalities and regions are some of the target groups of the planned communication events. In order to raise awareness on the topic of the euro, the Ministry of Finance and the BNB have already published on their websites information materials with questions and answers on this subject. These materials provide information on the euro area, the European Central Bank (ECB), the convergence criteria for introduction of the euro and the advantages it offers, as well as technical information on the exchange process and the conversion from Bulgarian levs to euro. A dedicated website on the euro is about to be put up, where it will be provided a detailed description of the benefits of the euro adoption, the good practices and experience of other countries that have introduced the euro, the ways of currency exchange, the period of dual display of prices, the security features of the euro banknotes and coins, etc. Bulgaria embarked on the path to euro adoption in July 2020 when the country joined the Exchange Rate Mechanism with the pegged exchange rate of BGN 1.95583 for EUR 1. Since October 2020 Bulgaria has been a participant in the Single Supervisory Mechanism (so-called banking union) and in the Single Resolution Mechanism. The significant banks in the country, which belong to large European banking groups, have been placed under the ECBs direct supervision, and the remaining banks are supervised by the BNB which follows the ECBs guidelines and takes the necessary measures to implement the ECBs legal acts in compliance with the applicable legal framework. The participation in these fundamental structures of the euro area ensures greater stability of, and confidence in, the banking sector in our country. The organisational, technical and regulatory activities associated with euro adoption have been running in accordance with the National Euro Changeover Plan of the Republic of Bulgaria adopted by the Council of Ministers in May 2022. A draft Law on the euro adoption has been prepared and it establishes the rules and procedures for introducing the euro in the country. This draft law stipulates that all accounts will be converted from Bulgarian levs to euro automatically and free of charge on the day of the introduction of the euro in Bulgaria. There are no reasons to expect any change in the fixed exchange rate of BGN 1.95583 for EUR 1, with which Bulgaria joined the Exchange Rate Mechanism nearly three years ago. During the first month after the euro adoption date, the lev and the euro will circulate together, both as legal tender. When this one-month period expires, the euro will become the sole official currency of our country. During the first six months after the euro adoption, banks and Bulgarian Posts Plc will exchange BGN banknotes and coins for euro free of charge, while the BNB will make such exchange free of charge for an unlimited period of time. The draft Law on the euro adoption will incorporate a consumer protection principle ensuring that the conversion of prices and other BGN currency amounts from levs to euro would not leave consumers in a worse financial situation than they would have been if the euro had not been introduced, as well as the necessary control and sanction mechanisms. A few of the basic arguments against the introduction of the euro state that the euro changeover might cause price rises, decreased incomes or impoverishment of the people. The unbiased data on, and surveys of, the economies that preceded us in joining the euro area, especially the Eastern European countries which are more comparable to Bulgaria, suggest quite the opposite. The Eurostat data on some countries that most recently joined the euro area show negligible inflation differences for the euro adoption year, ranging between 0.3% and 0.7% for Estonia and Latvia, whereas in Lithuania there even was deflation when comparing the harmonised index of consumer prices for the euro adoption year with the average annual value for the preceding 12 months. The same trend is also confirmed by the experience in Croatia which joined the euro area from the beginning of 2023. During the transition to the euro, the calculated impact on inflation in Croatia was low too  around 0.3% - 0.5% month-on-month increase, considering the January  April 2023 data on an average annual basis. In this regard, the concerns that the euro adoption will lead to significant inflation are unfounded and stem rather from insufficient awareness. The data indicate that, despite a temporary and feeble rise in some cases, inflation is decreasing steadily after the respective country joins the euro area. Over the first four months after euro changeover, the month-on-month inflation in Croatia shows a persistent decrease  from 12.7% in December 2022 to 8.9% in April this year. If we compare the latest data on inflation measured through the harmonised index of consumer prices as of April 2023, in the euro area it was 7%, while the inflation in the same period in Bulgaria was 14%, in Romania it was 13.1%, and in Hungary it was 20.8%. The growth of the average wage in the countries that joined the euro area before Bulgaria is also showing a strong upward trend. We can take a longer-term look at the impact in, for example, the countries that most recently joined the euro area  Lithuania (2015), Latvia (2014) and Estonia (2011). Five years before their entry in the euro area, the average monthly wage in these countries varied in the range between EUR 550 and EUR 700. When they joined the euro area, it was around EUR 700  EUR 800, i.e. over the five-year period before the euro adoption its growth has been between 5% in Latvia and 30% in Estonia. In 2022 the average wage in these countries ranged between EUR 1400 and EUR 1900, which is an increase between two and three times  from 92% in Latvia to 164% in Lithuania, compared to the corresponding euro adoption year. For comparison purposes, at the end of 2022 the average gross monthly wage in Bulgaria was EUR 995. The cited data suggest that the introduction of the euro boosts the economic development and the increase in peoples welfare. The full participation in the economic and monetary union creates prerequisites for full integration into the European structures and for reaping the maximum potential of the participation in the single European market, including by removing the need for conversion from levs to euro and eliminating transaction costs. The data and the experience of the countries that have joined the euro area earlier than us show that the adoption of the euro fosters real economic growth, competitiveness and investments, and the implications for the people involve a sustained development and convergence of incomes with the average European incomes. Such convergence runs faster when a country is part of the euro area. I wish the participants in the discussion interesting and productive work. ___________ HYPERLINK " " PAGE \* MERGEFORMAT 3

Title: Speech by Ms. Nina Stoyanova, Deputy Governor of the BNB, Head of the Banking Department, at the opening of the Finance Forum "Innovation", organized by the Bank of the Year Association, June 7, 2023
text: Speech by Ms Nina Stoyanova, BNB Deputy Governor in charge of the Banking Department, at the opening of the Financial Forum Innovations, organised by Association Bank of the Year, 7 June 2023 I would like to thank the organisers from the Association Bank of the Year for inviting me to open todays Financial Forum Innovations. Over the years this Forum has established itself as one of the most important events in the area of finance and payments. The financial sector in Europe and in our country is undoubtedly one of the areas where innovations are advancing most rapidly and have the greatest impact on the dynamics of products and services. Today we see fully digitalised banks, self-service zones, implementation of artificial intelligence, increasingly varied payment instruments and technologies. Developing competition, but also partnership between the Fintech sector and banks fosters the emergence of multiple new, convenient and secure financial and payment products. At the same time, the policies pursued by national and European regulators have led to a lasting and stable reduction in payment fraud. The data in the recently published report of the European Central Bank (ECB) on this subject, covering the period of 2020  2021, show that in 2021 card fraud in Europe, as a share of the total value of card payments, reached its lowest level since the start of such statistical data collection in 2008, i.e. less than 0.03%. More specifically, the value of card-not-present fraud (i.e. through virtual POS terminals) declined by 12% in 2021 compared to 2020 in light of the market-wide implementation of the strong customer authentication standards. Another vivid illustration is that fraud via counterfeit cards at physical terminals (e.g. in the form of using forged payment cards at shops and ATMs) declined by 42% in 2021 compared to 2020, and the mass implementation of the chip and PIN enhanced security standards almost eradicated such type of fraud in Europe. The payment infrastructure in Bulgaria has evolved significantly over the last few years with the aim to implement modern technological solutions and to ensure the security of payments. The preparations for the euro changeover have certainly catalysed and accelerated this process. Market players and the Bulgarian National Bank continue to work intensively on all the projects incorporated in the National Euro Changeover Plan of the Republic of Bulgaria. All the activities are running according to plan, and the payment infrastructure in the country is expected to be ready to join the euro area by the end of 2023. The project for ensuring full reachability within the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) for credit transfers in euro from/to Bulgaria will be brought to completion by the end of this year. Preparations are ongoing for the implementation of instant credit transfers in euro as a continuation of the already implemented instant credit transfers in levs. The migration of budget payments to the SEPA standards, planned to take place in October 2023, will finally bring the payment infrastructure in alignment with the SEPA standards. As a result, customers will be able to benefit from faster and more secure payment transactions. The innovations in the payment services segment are clearly visible in the statistical data that we have. For yet another year, the trend of increasing basic indicators of payment services, and mostly of those provided electronically, is confirmed. In 2022 the number of cashless customer payments conducted in the country rose by around 1/4th relative to the previous year. The number of payments with cards issued in Bulgaria went up by nearly 1/3rd compared to 2021. Also, there was impressive growth in the number of initiated e-money payments in 2022, by more than 40% compared to 2021. We can outline several segments whose development would have an impact on payment processes in the medium term. First of all, this is the development of central bank digital currencies. A 2021 survey of the Bank for International Settlements shows that nearly 90% of the central banks in the world are exploring the potential of digital currencies, and 14% are devising pilot projects. Especially interesting is the development of such a project in China over the last few years, where the digital renminbi is undergoing public testing in certain areas of the country. The development of central bank digital currencies is driven by significant factors, one of which is the fact that cash is being used less and less as a means of payment. Central banks should respond to the continuing digital transformation of the business and the evolution of payment instruments, and also to the possibility of global corporations with immense client bases developing their own private digital means of payment. With regard to the digital currency projects of central banks, the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund, Ms Kristalina Georgieva, says in one of her statements in 2022 that the history of money is entering a new chapter. As a future participant in the euro area, we are following the European Central Bank's digital euro project, whose exploratory phase ends in October this year. This project is taking on more and more concrete dimensions and it looks like it will continue to develop. Working groups have been established to develop rules (Rulebook) relating to the digital euro scheme, its use as a payment instrument, liquidity management, etc. Work is also underway on a specific legislative proposal of the European Commission on the digital euro, which may come up as early as the summer of this year. It is expected to clarify also the potential status of the digital euro as legal tender. In order to guarantee the function of financial intermediation that banks have in the modern economy, the implementation of a limit on the funds that individuals will be able to hold in a digital euro account with the central bank is being considered. The digital euro has the potential to create the basis for integrated European retail payment and cross-border settlement solutions, as well as many additional innovations  e.g. tokenised deposits, smart contracts, conditional payments, etc. Another important element on a global scale is the development of crypto-assets and their regulation. In the middle of May this year, the Council of the European Union finally adopted the final texts of the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA); thus the European institutions developed and adopted a large-scale and detailed legal framework for the crypto-assets market in Europe, having in mind that there are still very few attempts at regulation in this area. At the same time, a new Regulation on information accompanying transfers of funds and the transfer of certain crypto-assets was adopted, which will achieve better traceability of transfers of crypto-assets and anti-money laundering. The MiCA provisions on stablecoin crypto-assets will start to apply in July 2024, and the remaining regulations on general crypto-assets, which do not have a stabilisation mechanism of their value, and on crypto-asset service providers  in January 2025. Next, we expect the implementation of the measures envisaged in the Eurosystems Retail Payments Strategy, published by the ECB in 2021. An important aspect here is the development of instant payments in euro. One of the main objectives is to promote the creation of European retail payment solutions that are secure and efficient, and also as a response to the growing challenges to the European independence in the field of payments. The spread of instant payments in Europe is expected to continue, as is the establishment of infrastructure to accept instant payments initiated by customers via smartphone applications on physical POS terminals at merchants. In this regard, the so-called European Payments Initiative (EPI) was created, which aims to develop payment alternatives in Europe, including through a digital wallet based on instant payments. The review of the Second Payment Services Directive is also gathering serious speed, and after the directive has been into force for more than five years, a legislation package for the revision of PSD2 is expected to be announced in the summer of 2023. This package is expected to contain a revised Payment Services Directive (i.e. PSD3) and a proposal for a new Payment Services Regulation. In addition, a new legal framework for open finance will be developed, which will build on the existing regulations in the PSD2 on open banking, which shows good development, including in our country. The purpose of such a new legal framework would be to allow, with the customer's consent, their data falling outside the scope of PSD2 to be shared and reused by financial service providers to create new and improved services. The financial services and payments sector in Europe and in our country has traditionally been developing intensively and upwardly in recent years, driven by both innovation and the development of European regulations, which create a favourable environment for competition and security of consumers. The measures related to the introduction of the euro favour the faster and more efficient integration of the financial market infrastructures in our country with those in the euro area. I wish interesting and fruitful work to the participants in today's financial forum. ____________ HYPERLINK " Report on card fraud in 2020 and 2021, May 2023.
